sections.title: Dedication
sections.html:
This book is dedicated to the memory of my brother, Elder Kenneth N. Mbadinuju and my mother Agnes, through whose persistent preaching and prayers I came to know the Lord, both I and my family.

The book is also dedicated to all who with open minds seek to know the Truth of the Gospel.

sections.title: Foreword
sections.html:
It has been a great pleasure for me to read the script of this book and to realise that God has put His Hand on laymen who are ready and able to speak so clearly to their own people on matters so vital as this FALSE MEN and TRUE CHRISTIANS.

There are many thousands of men and women in Nigeria who need this book. They are sincerely seeking the Lord and also seeking the real truth. . . this book will answer many of their questions, and help them to realise how vital it is that all men should realise that “Except a man be born again he cannot see the Kingdom of God'

There are many church members who need this book and it is my prayer that the Holy Spirit Who alone can guide us into real truth and into the secrets of the Kingdom of God. . . will open their eyes to see what the Holy Spirit is saying to the churches in these last days. . . before it is too late for them to be awakened and brought to a saving knowledge of the truth.

It is very significant that after the Holy Spirit had led the aged Apostle JOHN to record and write the events of the book of the REVELATION that He should then also lead him to write and record the Gospel of John, for it seems clear that the Gospel of John is actually the last book recorded in the Bible. After realising the loss of spiritual life in the churches as stated so clearly in Revelation chapters two and three. . . and how dangerous was the spiritual condition of those christians who had 'lost their first love' and were in danger of also losing their salvation and rights to heaven. . . that Apostle John should make so definite a statement as he does in his Gospel Chapter three. . . on the need for NEW BIRTH.

He was making it clear that this fact was vital to the recovery of the spiritual condition of the churches. Like wise in Nigeria today, there is the vital need for all church members to realise that no matter how faithful they may be to their church duties or how well they are seeking to live a godly life. . . unless they are 'born again' by the Holy Spirit's work in their lives. . . they CANNOT see the Kingdom of Heaven, no matter how much they strive or work.

This book should also be read carefully by all christian workers who have been born again as they begin their christian lives but who have fallen into the mistake of thinking that what has been started in the 'spirit' can be finished and completed in the flesh. Many ministers, evangelists, workers are very busy trying to build the 'church' by human efforts and activities. This cannot be done. . . "Not by might . . . nor by power. . . but by MY SPIRIT Saith the Lord. . ."

The Holy Spirit alone can reveal the thoughts and mind of God. . . likewise He alone can do the work of God and for God. . . God is never going to allow any flesh to take the place of the Holy Spirit to do His work. 'No flesh can glory in His presence!' The flesh is quite incapable of finishing the glorious work of redemption which was started by the Spirit. . . So there is also need for all christian workers to study once again the truth. . ."That which is flesh is flesh and that which is spirit is SPIRIT" The two will never be mingled or used together by God.

I am sure the Holy Spirit will use this book to the end that many sincere church members will submit to the pressure of the Holy Spirit and yield themselves to His pleading to be 'born again' and to submit their wills to the Spirit of God so that they may be anointed for witnessing and ministry in the Spirit also.

May the Lord bless everyone who reads this book and seeks to yield themselves to the Spirit Himself. I warmly recommend it to all believers and unbelievers alike. . . it is a splendid contribution to the Christian witness of Nigerians for Nigerians.

S. G. Elton

(P.O. Box 113, Ilesha,

Oyo State, Nigeria).

sections.title: Preface
sections.html:
I thank God for the opportunity to write this book. There are some purposes which, believing God, shall be achieved by a careful and prayerful reading of this book. The major purpose is to emphasize the perfect and holy nature of God and to show that God created man in His image, after His own likeness and intended him to be perfect and holy as God Himself is.

However, through disobedience to the will and commandment of God, man sinned against God and therefore came short of the glory of God. Man was consequently sentenced to eternal death, both spiritually and physically, because the wages of sin is death; and the soul that sinneth it shall die. Sin is both the original sin of Adam which all men inherited, as well as the sins which we commit in our day to day living in our actions, behaviour, the thoughts and plans we hold and make in our hearts and minds, the words we speak, how we speak them, even the motive behind our actions and behaviour - all these things constitute sin if they are unrighteous, judged by the standard of God.

God in His infinite wisdom, mercy and goodness decided to punish every sinner, but because it is not the will of God that any of His creatures should perish but that everyone should come to repentance (2 Peter 3:9), He therefore gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life (John 3:16). This same Jesus who is both Lord and God, it is He who made heaven and earth and the sea and all that therein is, visible and invisible (John 1:3), and it is in Him we live and move and have our being. We are His offspring (Acts 17:28). He is our God; we are His people, the work of His hand, and the sheep of His pasture. And today if you will hear His voice, even through this writing, harden not your heart (Psalm 95:6-8). Accept Him, believe Him, receive Him because He is our all in all; without Him we can do nothing (John 15:5). His name has been highly exalted and given above all names, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father (Phil. 2:9-11).

So the key to entering the Kingdom of God is Jesus. For He said, "I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me" (John 14:6). Similarly, the condition for seeing the Kingdom of God is to be born again. For Jesus said, "Except a man be born again, he cannot see the Kingdom of God" (John 3:3). But there are people today who have rejected Christ Jesus as Lord and their personal Saviour, and instead they worship other gods and dead human beings. Such people should read again the Word of God as written in John 14:6.

Also there are other people who say they have received Jesus as their Lord and personal Saviour and they attend church regularly, give alms, and they are very active in church work and organisations. Some of them are ministers, pastors, bishops, arch-bishops, teachers and so on. But unfortunately, such people would tell you that they are just christians, that they are not born again, and they do not want to be. They say, "if after I have served God in all these duties in the church and He cast me into hell because I am not born again, then I will take it as the will of God for me." No my dear reader, it is not the will of God that anyone should perish, but that everyone should come to repentance (2 Peter 3:9). And again God said that the times of this ignorance He winked at, but now commands all men everywhere to repent. (Acts 17:30). The Word of God is that "except a man be born again, he cannot see the Kingdom of God."

Whoever accepts the Word of God and lives by it will be saved. Whoever does not know about the Word, or he hears it and refuses or neglects to live by it will surely perish. This is the main purpose of writing this book. Please heed this warning! It does not profit you anything that you should waste your life, your time, your money, or patronizing a church when you have not been born again or saved. Being baptised is not the new birth, receiving the Holy Communion is not the new birth, being married in the church and belonging to all church committees does not confer the new birth on you. Going on pilgrimage to Rome or Jerusalem, and worshipping and kissing relics and religious images and emblems will not save any one. Jesus said, "except a man be born again, he cannot see the Kingdom of God."

After someone has been born again, God being perfect and holy, tells us to "Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord" (Heb. 12:14). It is not enough that a person has been born again because "many are called but few are chosen" (Matt. 22:14). But it is important that if you say you love the Lord, you must keep His commandments (John 14:15).

This book is important in many respects, one of which is its 'mirror' function. It is not enough for someone to say that he is born again, he must manifest the fruits of repentance. This book examines seven evidences or manifestations of the new birth. If one says he is born again but he does not manifest all of the evidences discussed here, there would be a question mark to his claim. The seven are just examples which I was guided to select. This book also discusses the steps to receive the new birth, as well as what salvation means and how to receive it.

The book contains chapters on the Last Day Judgment. There is a discussion of the Judgment of the believers or the born again christian at the Judgment Seat of Christ. The reward each christian gets will be decided there. There is also judgment of the unbelievers, those who rejected Christ, and those who attended church without being born again - these ones will be judged at the Great White Throne and their sentence will be eternal stay and torment in hell fire. The ways to avoid hell and being judged at the Great White Throne are all discussed in this book.

We also see in this book that the Lord Jesus Christ will be the Judge of the whole world (John 5:22), just as He is God who created everything in heaven, on earth, and the sea, everything in them, visible and invisible (John 1:3 and 10). The Word of God is freely and abundantly used to show that Jesus is Lord, that He is God.

Then I have added a personal testimony of how I received my new birth to show that what God has done for me He is able to do for you and for others because Jesus is the same yesterday, and today, and forever (Heb. 13:8). There is a purpose for discussing my early Christian up-bringing; my educational background and accomplishments, and also the positions and titles I held before I came to know Jesus as Lord and my personal Saviour. I recounted all these things so that like Paul in Philippians 3:4-8 I could also say that I "do count them but dung, that I may win Christ".

FALSE MEN and TRUE CHRISTIANS is a book which everyone who seeks the truth of the Gospel should find useful. For the unbeliever who is the transgressor, it is a book of salvation which should lead him to Christ. For the nominal Christian who still lives in his sins, it is a book of deliverance if he will heed the warning of Christ how He said "ye must be born again" (John 3:3, 7).

Those who, despite the witness of the Holy Spirit today, and the evidence of the Gospel, the written Word of God, still doubt, disbelieve, and are double-minded, only seek to make God a liar or to prove Him false. But such people cannot succeed, because assuming they still do not believe, shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? The Bible answers, "God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar" (Romans 3:4). Therefore the unbelieving, doubting and the double-minded people are FALSE MEN because "That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation..." (Heb. 6:18 also Numbers 23:19).

Lastly, the book will be useful for the TRUE CHRISTIANS who in obedience to the Word of God are born again, and are now working out their salvation with fear and trembling. Chapter 7 which is a portrait of the TRUE CHRISTIANS will be of particular interest to them.

May you be richly blessed as you read the whole of this book.

C. C. MBADINJU

Oderа Chambers,

Onitsha.

sections.title: God's Word and Man's Wisdom
sections.html:
The word of God bears true testimony that in the beginning God created the heaven and the earth (Gen. 1:1). God also created man (Gen. 1:26 and 2:7) and created woman (Gen. 2:18 and 22).

The great purpose of God in His creation was for man to take dominion over all the earth and to rule. Man was indeed born to rule (Gen. 1:28-31). And one of the primary purposes of God in creating man in His own image after His likeness (Gen. 1:26) was for God to have fellowship with him (Gen. 3:8).

And in return for all these God's favours, the whole duty of man was fixed at two things: to fear God and to keep His commandments (Ecclesiastes 12:13).

The first commandment God gave man was: "Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shall not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shall surely die". Remember as we have seen already that the whole duty of man is to fear God to keep His commandments.

Surely if man at this stage had obeyed and kept every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God he would have remained till today the pure and blessed creature of God without death, without sufferings, without trials and tribulations, without wars, without scarcity.

But Satan, the evil one, came into the scene and has remained with man since then for better or for worse.

Although the commandment of God was clear and unequivocal that man would die the day he ate the tree of the knowledge of good and evil but the devil said: "Ye shall not surely die: For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods knowing good and evil" (Gen. 3:4-5). Adam, the first man, and Eve the first woman therefore believed the lie of the devil and disbelieved the truth of God and thereupon God punished them with the punishment He had promised which is death.

So we see that the immediate result of man's sin or his disobedience against God's commandment is death (Romans 6:23). This death comes in three forms: (1) physical death which is the separation of man's body from his spirit (Gen. 3:19), (2) spiritual death which is separation of man from fellowship with God (Isaiah 59:2), and (3) eternal death which is separation of man from God for ever and ever which means living in hell (Revelation 20:11-15).

I will deal with this subject in more details later but meanwhile it is important to underscore the point that it was Satan's lie and man's free-will acceptance of it that separated man from God and ended the fellowship between the two.

Today, Satan is still telling man lies about himself and about God and man is still believing the devil and being deceived, and therefore man's separation from God continues. Today, as in the days of old, God is telling us: "I am the Lord, and there is no other. I the Lord speak the truth, I declare what is right" (Isaiah 45:19). The devil tells us it is not true that the Lord had spoken.

The philosophers and 'wise' men today tell us that there is nothing like truth or absolute truth; that truth, like love, is in the eye of the beholder.

Even such a highly placed Roman ruler and judge, Pontius Pilate, at a very critical moment of life and death decision was blinded enough not to know the truth and he asked our Lord: "What is truth?" (John 18:38). But the truth of the matter is that whenever a man is blinded by Satan he would never know the truth because God is truth, even as the Lord Jesus Christ said: "I am the Way, the Truth and the Life" (John 14:6).

The devil will forever deny the truth of this statement just as the unbelievers who are disciples of the devil deny this truth today.

Similarly God said to man that the meek shall inherit the earth" (Matt. 5:5) and commanded man saying: "But seek ye first the Kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you" (Matt. 6:33; Luke 12:31). But instead the devil tells man that it is only the strong, the mighty, and the troublesome who shall inherit the earth, and not the meek.

Rather than first seek the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, the devil tells man that the most reasonable and natural thing would be for God, if He is really God, to first add all the things he promised us: good house, car, money, wealth, children, and then and only then shall we "seek the Kingdom of God and his righteousness".

Does this not explain why nothing seems to go well with man today because we fail to seek after the will of God? Man is more willing to accept the lie of the devil than he is ready to live by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God (Matt. 4:4).

Recently, I was witnessing to a colleague, a lawyer, who holds a Ph.D. in international law and jurisprudence. He is certainly very well read. He complained that "my people"—meaning the members of the church where I fellowship—disturb him every evening with our songs and musical instruments. He said that one reason he does not like that kind of Church is because we act like children.

Then I told him what our Lord Jesus Christ said that "whosoever shall not receive the Kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein" (Mark 10:15). Then my friend laughed and said, "Well, that cannot be true... Jesus Christ cannot say anything like that".

My friend then used his legal and logical mind to analyse the issue. He said, and correctly too, that when Christ was only about twelve years of age He went into the temple and engaged the rabbis, the scribes, the lawyers and learned men of the time in argument. He listened to them and asked them questions and all who heard him marvelled at his wisdom, knowledge and understanding (Luke 2:41-52).

Then my friend asked: Can Jesus who showed such wonderful intelligence and maturity at the age of twelve tell his disciples who were older than himself that they must receive the Kingdom of God like "little children" before they can enter therein?

Every effort failed to explain to him that Christ merely taught that humility, purity, obedience and sincerity of heart as can be found in little children are qualities of lifestyle in the Kingdom of God.

My friend is obviously learned and "wise", but he is not wise in the things of God.

God said: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent. Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the disputer of this world? Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?" (1 Cor. 1:19-20).

Paul said: "We preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumbling-block, and unto the Greeks foolishness. But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God" (1 Cor. 1:23-24).

The arrogance, pride, and stiffneckness of the educated and elite class as well as their opposition to Christ and the Gospel did not start today.

For example, we read of one arrogant lawyer who stood up to our Lord and tempted Him with a question on what to do for him to inherit eternal life (Luke 10:25 and 29).

At another occasion our Lord had to pronounce curse upon the lawyers (representing all educated unbelievers); Our Lord said: "Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers". "Woe unto you lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge; ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered" (Luke 11:46 and 52).

Our Lord similarly put a curse upon the other educated class of His day and said: "Woe unto you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the Kingdom of heaven against men, for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in" (Matt. 23:13).

This was a classic case of a "dog in the manger". The dog would not go in and would not allow anyone else to go in.

It is noteworthy that the educated class has always had a privileged status in the society. They form the ruling elite, the propertied and wealthy class, and because of this they have naturally become a proud group.

It is not difficult therefore to see the reason for the conflict between them and our Lord Jesus because God had said that He would "scatter the proud in the imagination of their hearts" (Luke 1:51).

Very few today would measure up to the education and upbringing of Paul, the Apostle.

But in spite of that, the Apostle accepted Jesus Christ as his Lord and personal Saviour and became a tool to propagate the gospel to every nook and corner of the known world in his day.

In his own time, Saul, who later became Paul, was a highly learned man in law, history, and culture. He was surely among the highest ranking intelligentsia in his time. He belonged to the most respectable cultural and learned group. He performed their membership rites, and received all the honours and privileges attached to every one of the high positions he occupied.

Paul himself in all modesty enumerated the privileges he had in life in his letter to the Philippians in which he said that he 'was circumcised, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew; as touching the law, a Pharisee, concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless".

After listing these credentials and qualifications which distinguished him as unique and outstanding in his accomplishments, Paul shocked every one when he said: "But what things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ. . . I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ". (Philippians 3:5-8).

What therefore must be apparent to the educated class, the logicians, the philosophers and the 'wise' men of this world is that "by wisdom men knew not God" (1 Cor. 1:21). God in His infinite wisdom and knowledge "had chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the things which are mighty" (1 Cor. 1:27). It is impossible for man to reason out God because the Omnipotent Lord is unsearchable in all his judgments, and His ways are past finding out (Rom. 11:33).

God also told the sons of men saying: "My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways. . . for as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts" (Isaiah 55:8-9).

Furthermore, a man who is yet unchanged, and not in the spirit, cannot understand the ways of God because God is spirit and those who worship Him must worship Him in spirit and in truth (John 4:23). And also the unspiritual man does not receive the gifts of the spirit of God, for they are folly to him, and he is not able to understand them because they are spiritually discerned (1 Cor. 2:14).

From what we have said so far it is clear that man cannot reason out God, and man because of his sin was separated from God since the fall of Adam.

As the Prophet Isaiah said: "Your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you so that he does not hear" (Isaiah 59:2). And it is said in the Book of Psalms that "If I regard iniquity in my heart the Lord will not hear me" (Psalm 66:18).

sections.title: What is Sin
sections.html:
There are some people who say that they have committed no sin and therefore they have nothing to repent of. According to them, they:

  • live a decent life;

  • try to keep the ten commandments;

  • go to church every Sunday;

  • pray every day;

  • give alms to the poor;

  • they do not trouble their neighbour.

This is only part of the same devil's lie. God on His own part said that "All have sinned and come short of the glory of God" (Rom. 3:23) and the Psalmist said:

"The LORD looks down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there are any that act wisely, that seek after God. They have all gone astray; they are all alike corrupt; there is none that does good, no, not one" (Psalm 14:2-3).

Isaiah said that "All we like sheep have gone astray, we have turned every one to his own way" (Isaiah 53:6). And John the Apostle wrote: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make God a liar, and his word is not in us" (1 John 1:8-10).

There are two types of sins being considered here. One is the original sin which Adam and Eve committed through their disobedience to God's commandment. Although it was Adam who sinned but we inherited not only his blood but also his sin.

We all have the blood of Adam in us as well as his sin which he committed and that is why Paul, the Apostle wrote: "Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned" (Rom. 5:12).

The second type of sin which separates us from God are the day to day wrongdoings we commit. Many people have inquired to know what actually constitutes sin. But simply put "all wrongdoing is sin" (1 John 5:17), which means that whatever does not proceed from faith is sin (Rom. 14:23).

Our Lord Jesus said that "From within, out of the heart of man, come evil thoughts, fornication, theft, murder, adultery, coveting, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, envy, slander, pride, foolishness. All these evil things come from within, and they defile a man" (Mark 7:21-23).

In his Epistle to the Romans, St. Paul listed other day-to-day sins such as "being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity, whisperers, backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, without understanding, covenant-breakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful".

The Bible warns us that it is not only those who commit these sins who will be judged, it also says that those who aid and abet them and associate themselves with such evil doers will also be punished, for according to St. Paul, "Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them". (Rom. 1:29-32)

Paul in his letter to the Galatians also reproduced another list of sins which if we commit condemn us before God. These include all the works of flesh: "adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness, idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, sedition, heresies, envyings, murder, drunkenness, revellings" (Galatians 5:19-21).

And John in Revelations added the following: "fear, unbelief, the abominable, murderers, whoremongers, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone" (Rev. 21:8).

In Exodus 20:3-17 the following sins are listed: idolatry, cursing, sabbath breaking, disrespect to parents, murder, adultery, stealing, lying, and covetousness. In 1 Cor. 6:9-10 the sins condemned include effeminate, masturbation, drunkards, revilers, and extortioners.

In 1 Timothy 1:9-11 six sins are listed: lawlessness, disobedience, unholiness, profanity, whoremonger, kidnapping; and Colossians 3:5-8 condemns inordinate affection, anger, wrath, malice, blasphemy and filthy communication. For other sins condemned in the Bible see the following: Matt 15:18-20; 1 Cor. 10:7-10; 2 Cor. 12:20-21; Eph. 5:1-8; 2 Tim. 3:1-5

sections.title: Hell: A Place of Torment for Sinners
sections.html:
Now God said that all sinners and liars shall have their part in the lake of fire, that is hell. Ezekiel the Prophet said that the "soul that sinneth, it shall die" (Ezekiel 18:4) and St. Paul said in Romans that "the wages of sin is death" (Rom. 6:23).

But given these clear and unmistakable Words of God which says that every sinner shall be punished with death in hell fire, the Satan still lies and convinces many today that there is nothing like hell. Just like Satan told Eve, "Thou shalt not surely die" the devil is also telling people today that there is surely no hell. Adam and Eve believed the devil and they died; and so shall die all who believe Satan today, unless such people repent and turn to God.

But whether or not man believes God there is hell, and because man has chosen to go there, God has enlarged it as it is said in Isaiah that, "hell hath enlarged herself, and opened her mouth without measure" (Isaiah 5:14); and in Proverbs 27:20 it is said that "hell and destruction are never full". Hell is a place of punishment (Matt 25:46); a place of torment (Luke 16:23); a place of fire (Matt 13:42, 50; Rev. 20:15).

The 'wise' men of our day who argue that there is no hell, that God is so kind and so merciful that He will not cast any of His creatures into such a horrible place as hell should remember that the same Bible that speaks of the love of God also speaks of the justice and holiness of God. He is both loving and just.

These doubters say that even if there is hell, at worst sinners would be cast into it and they die only once and for all. But unfortunately for these people, the Bible clearly states that the Lake of Fire is eternal and that those thrown into it will be tormented day and night for ever and ever.

The book of Revelation says, "And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever" (Rev. 20:10). This means that those sinners being tormented in the hell fire shall not die; they shall live for ever and be tormented for ever.

I now refer you to the rich man, a sinner who refused to repent and who died and went to hell and from there he begged the poor but repentant Lazarus in Paradise to get a drop of water to "cool my tongue because I am tormented in this flame" (Luke 16:22-24).

The soul of every man shall live for ever, either in hell fire or in heaven, and we must all make the choice today while we are still alive, whether we shall repent and go to heaven, or remain in our sin and spend our eternity in this Lake of Fire.

The Bible clearly teaches that the wicked and sinners who reject Christ will be cast into hell, thus, "The wicked shall be turned into hell, and all the nations that forget God" (Psalm 9:17)

Even our Lord Jesus Christ had occasions to teach about hell and hell fire. We know that Christ created everything according to the word of God which said that "all things were made by him: and without him was not anything made that was made" (John 1:3).

So we can see from this passage that Christ himself made hell for He created all things. Therefore anything our Lord said about the subject of hell and hell fire is authoritative and final.

Very often we think of our Lord Jesus as one who is "meek and lowly" with a compassionate heart for His children, who shows sympathy and mercy for the disabled, the poor, and the infirm, and who labours to heal and to comfort. Clearly Christ came to seek and to save that which is lost, but His work of mercy ends with those who accept Him as their Lord and Saviour, and He warned about the serious consequences of not hearing Him or believing Him.

Our Lord warned: "And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do. But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell, yea, I say unto you, Fear him" (Luke 12:4-5).

Furthermore, Christ's first teaching on this subject was during His sermon on the Mount. In Matthew's Gospel Chapter 5 verse 22 Christ warned against the danger of "hell fire". In verses 29 and 30 He warned about the danger of anybody being "cast into hell".

These passages not only reflect the horrible notion and state of hell but also assure that there is a place like that.

Note also that what our Lord said in Luke 12:5 above shows clearly that hell exists not in this life but in the life after this. And to those "wise" men who take exception to the notion that the good Lord will torture the wicked, it is important to point out that it is not God who will torture, but one's conscience and memory will do the torturing in hell.

So we have to decide today whether it is better to believe the lie of the devil, or to believe the "Word of God". Peter and the other apostles agreed that "we ought to obey God rather than men" (Acts 5:29).

Because hell is a place of torment it is not expected that any man will get chance to enjoy anything while in it. There will be no communication and no friendship in hell. People there will be able to pray although the prayer will not be granted (Luke 16:24); and they will also be able to recognise each other but there will be no opportunity for cooperation or collaboration.

And no person who has entered into hell has any more opportunity to repent, or to come out from there for another place (Luke 16:22-31).

Therefore "christians" who now live in sin and who hope that after death they would go to purgatory, and after a short stay and torment there would be brought out and be taken to heaven should forget it. They are just being deceived because there is simply no truth like that.

Such teaching is not in the Bible. It is only part of the same devil's lie. Nobody shall be given a second chance after death according to Hebrews 9:27.

If sin is found in you at death which takes you to either purgatory, sheol, hades, hell, the pit, the lake of fire, gehena, or tartarus, (all these names mean the same), please take note that you will be there for eternity and will be tormented for ever.

Many "christians" today in fact look forward to their "brief" stay in purgatory. Such people deserve to be pitied!

The Bible is clear on this point for Isaiah said: "For the grave cannot praise thee, death cannot celebrate thee: they that go down into the pit (hell) cannot hope for thy truth" (Isaiah 38:18). St. Paul also said in Hebrews that "it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment" (Heb. 9:27).

There will therefore be no second chance: absolutely none!

Let us remember that hell is not inhabited by only the grossly wicked people like the murderers, sexual perverts, idolaters, sorcerers, liars and their likes. Rather, it will be inhabited also by those we have regarded as good, clean, moral people, "christians" and other religionists whose main fault was that they rejected Jesus Christ as their Lord and Saviour.

Perhaps you will be wondering why "christians" have been included in this list. The reason will be made clear later because it is not all who call Jesus "Lord, Lord, shall enter into the Kingdom of God."

It should be realised that hell as a creation of God was not initially meant for man. The Lake of Fire was rather intended to be a place of eternal punishment for supernatural beings like the devil and the fallen angels.

In Matthew's Gospel it is said, "Depart from Me, ye cursed into everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels" (Matt. 25:41).

Angels of God were created before the earth, and the Bible says that a great number of these Angels at a point in time rebelled against God under the leadership of Lucifer who was said to be the greatest being created (Ezekiel 28:15; Isaiah 14:12-15)

These Angels who rebelled against God were all rounded up and are now in assylum or hell awaiting final judgment of God. This agrees with the Scripture in Jude 1:6 which says that "the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day". And similarly,

Peter the Apostle said "For if God did not spare the angels who sinned, but cast them down to hell and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved for judgment..." (2 Peter 2:4). If angels who sinned are now in hell, "reserved for judgment", what is man that he should escape the same judgment if he fails to repent of his sins and accept Jesus Christ as Lord and Saviour.

So, although the hell fire was not originally meant for man but for the angels who rebelled, the Lake of Fire has however been prepared and enlarged to receive mankind who refuse to accept the redemptive plan of God in not accepting Jesus Christ as the Lord and Saviour.

So the rebellious angels together with sinful mankind will have their part in the Lake of Fire where they will be tormented for ever and ever (Rev. 20:11-15).

sections.title: The Way to Avoid Hell
sections.html:
We have seen from above that no man living can say that he has no sin (1 John 1:8-10). The question is what man should do to escape the penalty of sin which is eternal death in the hell fire (Rom. 6:23).

It is absolutely important that no human being should continue to justify himself and claim that he has no sin. Rather, it is better that everyone should humble oneself and in a penitent heart say with the Psalmist: "And enter not into judgment with thy servant: for in thy sight shall no man living be justified" (Psalm 143:2).

All we need to do is to approach God with a penitent heart and confess our sins. We must confess and forsake every sin we have ever committed and God will forgive them all because he has so promised saying: "Come now, and let us reason together... though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool" (Isaiah 1:18).

The Lord God said, "As I live... I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his way and live" (Ezekiel 33:11).

God is not willing that any one should perish, but that all should come to repentance (2 Peter 3:9). God also said that, the times of ignorance, and the times we lived in sin without knowing the Word of God, and the will of God, that He is prepared to forget them and has infact forgiven them.

But "God now commands all men everywhere to repent" (Acts 17:30). He said, "Repent therefore, and turn again, that your sins may be blotted out" (Acts 3:19).

John the Apostle went further and assured that, "If any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world" (1 John 2:1-2).

It should be said however that the promise of God in this passage is made only to those who have received Jesus as their Lord and personal Saviour because the Epistle of John was written to believers in Christ, and not to unbelievers and the unregenerated.

But we are meanwhile talking about unbelievers, that is, people who do not believe the Lordship of Jesus Christ, as well as the "church-goers" who attend church regularly but still live in sin.

To escape eternal condemnation in hell fire, all sinners and all unbelievers need only to call upon the name of the Lord and they will be saved (Acts 2:21; Rom. 10:15). Salvation from sin is the only condition for anyone to enter into God's Kingdom and to receive the promise of eternal life. And salvation itself is nothing that anyone can work for or earn from his labours.

Paul the Apostle said that "by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: not of works, lest any man should boast" (Ephesians 2:8-9).

The Word of God tells us that the "just shall live by faith" (Habakkuk 2:4, Rom. 1:17, Gal. 3:11, Heb. 10:38) and not by works. But there are some 'wise' men today who say that their good works will be enough to see them through.

They quote the Bible that "God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son" (John 3:16), and they therefore conclude that they can claim the love of God and be saved by giving alms to the poor, contributing to harvest and bazaar sales, and serving in Church building committees.

But the truth of the matter is that the works any man does before he is saved by grace profits him nothing. God does not accept any work except the work of faith.

No man's work can purchase righteousness for him because as Isaiah said, "We are all as unclean thing, and all our righteousness are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind have taken us away" (Isaiah 64:6).

And writing to the Corinthian Church Paul drove the point nearer home saying, "Although I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not love, it profiteth me nothing" (1 Cor. 13:3).

Now this love is the kind that made God give His only begotten Son to die for our sins (John 3:16). It is both love of God, and love from God. This "love suffereth long, and is kind; it envieth not and vaunteth not itself; it is not puffed up and seeketh not her own; it is not easily

Here is the text from these pictures, in order:

provoked and thinketh not evil, it rejoiceth not in iniquity but rejoiceth in the truth; it beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things, and it never faileth" (1 Cor. 13:4-8).

An unregenerated spirit of a "christian" not yet born-again could never attain to this kind of love, and any works not done out of this love will be an abomination unto God. Although James in his Epistle properly wrote that "faith without works is dead" (James 2:20), he was not infact writing to the unbelievers because no unbeliever has faith. Faith as we know comes from hearing and hearing the word of God (Rom. 10:17).

If a person has not heard the word of God, or he hears it and believeth not, he would have no faith, no love, and no salvation. Whatever good works a person does before he has accepted Jesus Christ as his Lord and personal Saviour, only amount to a waste of his time and resources. They will profit him nothing.

God cannot be bribed with good works; what He demands from us is not sacrifice, but obedience to His word. Any sacrifice of our time, money, effort, even our bodies (Rom. 12:1) will be acceptable to God only after we have given our heart to Him because God pleads with us saying: "My son, give me thine heart" (Proverbs 23:26).

Our heart is much more precious to the Lord than fine gold. And to fear God and keep His commandments are more to be desired than gold, even fine gold (Psalm 19:9-10). We are reminded that God is not "worshipped with men's hands as though he needed anything seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things" (Acts 17:25).

So far, we have talked about hell as a place of torment which God has prepared for:-

  1. those who refused to believe in Jesus Christ as their Lord and Saviour and,

  2. those who believe but they cannot live the life; they live in sin,

  3. those who believed but later fell away from faith according to Hebrews 6:4-6.

So there are three types of people that will spend eternity in the hell fire: the unbelievers who are the transgressors, the believers or "church-goers" who live in sin, and believers or christians who backslid or fell away from faith and thus forsook the Lord. God said in His Word that all these three categories of people will be consumed (Isaiah 1:28).

But these transgressors, sinners and backsliders can still be saved if only they can repent today and turn away from their wickedness and return to God.

God has already promised that when a wicked man shall turn away from his wickedness that he has committed and do that which is lawful and right, he shall save his soul alive. (Ezekiel 18:27). So with regard to Sin, Punishment, and Forgiveness, the Bible has the following to say:

  1. God has no pleasure in the death of the wicked: it can be a wicked man who has not repented or one who has repented, lived for God for a time, and then gone back into sin.

  2. The wicked must turn from his wickedness to live.

  3. The wicked man is invited and commanded to turn from his wickedness or he will die in his sins and be lost.

  4. The righteousness of the righteous shall not even deliver such a man if he returns to sin.

  5. In the day that a righteous man goes back into sin he will incur the penalty of the broken law, and be separated from God as all other sinners are.

  6. Past righteousness will not save a righteous man when he transgresses and becomes a sinner again.

  7. The wickedness of the wicked will not damn his soul if and when he repents and turns from his wickedness to serve God and live in righteousness.

  8. God is no respecter of persons, He will not save the wicked until he repents and turns from sin to live right; and He will not continue to save the righteous man if he turns from his righteousness and lives in sin.

  9. All the righteousness of the righteous will not be remembered to cause God to excuse him in the day that he sins; for his iniquity that he commits he will die.

  10. When God says to the righteous that he will surely live if he continues in righteousness, or die if he goes back into sin, that is what is meant.

  11. When God says to the wicked that he will die, and he turns from his sins to do that which is lawful and right, then he will live and that is what is meant.

  12. All the sins of the wicked will not be remembered and mentioned to him to damn his soul when he turns from them to do that which is lawful and right; he will surely live.

  13. When the righteous turns from his righteousness and commits sins, he will even die thereby.

  14. When the wicked turns from his wickedness to do that which is lawful and right, he will live thereby.

Having seen the kind of future which hell holds for the unbelievers and sinners and having seen that the only way to escape hell is to repent today and be "born-again", it is very important also to have a look at a place called Heaven where those who believe in Jesus Christ as their Lord and Saviour will spend their eternity.

sections.title: Heaven: A Prepared Place for Prepared People
sections.html:
Just as hell was created by our Lord Jesus Christ so is heaven created by Him because, as we saw already, "All things were made by him; and without him was not anything made that was made" (John 1:3). Heaven basically is the home of the Lord, our God, "Our Father, which art in heaven..." (Matt. 6:9). There are three heavens:

  • the atmospheric heaven which we can see;

  • the space where the space ships go; and

  • the home or throne of God.

According to Isaiah the Prophet, "Thus saith the Lord, the heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool" (Isaiah 66:1). Heaven is also called the Kingdom of God and of Christ (Ephesians 5:5); a place of rest (Heb. 4:9); a paradise (11 Cor. 12:4); and it is called the Father's House, "In my father's house are many mansions... I go to prepare a place for you... that where I am there ye may be also" (John 14:2-3).

Heaven is described as a high place (Isaiah 57:15), a holy place (Psalm 20:6), a happy place (Rev. 7:17), a place without death, tears, sorrow, crying or pain (Rev. 21:4); it is a place without night or darkness (Rev. 22:3-5), a place without hunger, thirst and excessive heat (Rev. 7:16).

And as for those who will inherit heaven, they are the chosen, select few, known by God before the foundation of this world was laid.

Those who will never enter the heaven include: the devil (Rev. 20:1), thieves (Luke 12:33), the fearful, the unbelieving, the abominable, murderers, whoremongers, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars (Rev. 21:8).

Not to enter into heaven also are all those transgressors and sinners listed in Mark 7:21-23), Galatians 5:19-21, and Romans 1:29-32), Exodus 20:3-17, 1 Cor. 6:9-10, 1 Tim. 1:9-11. Matt. 15:18-20; 1 Cor. 10:7-10; 2 Cor. 12:20-21; Eph. 5:1-8, 2 Tim. 3:1-5.

But those to inherit life for ever and ever in heaven are: God the Father Himself (Matt. 6:9); Christ Jesus, who already is sitting at the right hand of God, the Father, following His ascension (Acts 3:21); Angels (Matt. 18:10, 26:53); Enoch and Elijah who were bodily translated there (Genesis 5:24); all who died believing and trusting in Jesus as Lord and Saviour, and all who are alive and remain in faith when Our Lord Jesus appears in the air. (1 Thess. 4:14-17).

All who would be allowed entry into heaven include "anyone who leads a blameless life and is truly sincere.

Anyone who refuses to slander others, does not listen to gossip, never harms his neighbours, speaks out against sin, criticizes those committing it, commends the faithful followers of the Lord, keeps a promise even it it ruins him, does not crush his debtors with high interest rates, and refuses to testify against the innocent despite the bribes offered him" (Psalm 15:1-5 Living Bible Translation).

Furthermore, heaven shall receive "he that hath clean hands, and a pure heart; who hath not lifted up his soul unto vanity, nor sworn deceitfully" (Psalm 24:4-5).

Heaven has been variously described: as a place of perfect satisfaction with a perfect leisurely comfort (Rev. 22:1-2); a place of perfect provision where everything is good and abundantly provided (Rev. 22:2); a place of perfect sinlessness (Rev. 22:3); a place of perfect government, a place ruled by God, the just One, and the Lamb (Rev. 22:3); a place of perfect communion and a place of perfect possession (Rev. 22:4), a place of perfect glory (Rev. 22:5).

The question that needs to be dealt with concerns the conditions attached to entry into heaven: what preparations have to be made by candidates for heaven since heaven is a prepared place for prepared people.

Heaven is not a place anyone can walk in by chance, or by accident.

If anyone enters there through the "back-door" without wearing the "garment of righteousness, truth, and holiness", his sins will find him out (Matt. 22:11-13).

In any case there is no doubt at all that an unbeliever will find heaven too uncomfortable because of its holiness. Therefore preparation is an absolute condition for entering heaven.

A story was once told of a King who gave a "cap of honour" to the best clown (that is, the best or biggest fool) in his Kingdom. While the King was on his death bed the clown came to see him and he asked the King what preparations he had made for going to heaven.

The King said "none" Then in a most solemn and ironical manner the clown placed the "cap of honour" on the King's head and said, "you must then wear this 'cap of honour'; you are the best and biggest fool".

It is only a fool who cannot in his life time prepare for the place he would spend his eternity.

The things of Heaven can be likened to the things of the University here on earth. There are entry requirements into a University. It is not a place any person can get up and enter for a study.

A person must be properly admitted after he has met with the basic entry qualifications. If someone is not so qualified he is refused entry or admission. If in the middle of his course he is found to have gained entry with false certificates and documents, which means that he came in through the "back door", he would be dismissed and the University may even take a criminal legal action against him.

But if someone is academically qualified and he has been properly admitted into the University he then pursues his normal course of study. He works hard to win honours in his course.

But instead of applying for a University admission a person may decide to study on his own. He may take tuition courses and attend evening classes. Even if he studies for ten years instead of four years as required by a University and even if he has become very knowledgeable and educated by these outside studies, he would still not receive any certificate or degree from any University.

To receive a degree from a University he must first be admitted, and he must also finish a course of studies successfully. If he finishes the course with honours he would then be awarded an honours degree. That would be his reward.

Similarly, entering into heaven and receiving a reward is like entering a University and receiving a degree.

There are entry requirements for heaven and they include the new birth. Christ said, "ye must be born-again" (John 3:7). Then after salvation one must "follow peace with all men, and holiness without which no man shall see the Lord" (Heb. 12:14).

If you love Christ, you must keep His commandments (John 14:15). If one enters through the "back door" without meeting with the entry requirements, Christ would do to him according to the story in Matt. 22:11-13.

After someone has taken the proper steps to be born again and has become spirit filled, he then has faith which he begins to manifest by his works since faith without works is dead (James 2:17, 20). On the last day of judgment his works will be judged and Christ will give him reward or crowns according to what he did in his body, whether it was good or bad (2 Cor. 5:10).

Like the person who studied on his own without attending any University and who received no certificate or degree for his studies, any person who does works of righteousness such as giving alms to the poor, regular attendance to church, contributions to church work and things like that) while he is not yet a born again christian would have all those personal sacrifices of his time and money nullified and counted as a wasted effort (Isaiah 64:6).

When the person dies he would still go to hell because he was not born again according to John 3:3; and then all his good works which he supposedly did would not help him, they would attract no reward just like the man who studied privately and because he never was admitted into the University, all his efforts were wasted as he receive no degree. Heaven therefore is a prepared place for prepared people.

Paul said that a runner should run so as to obtain a prize (1 Cor. 9:24). But he warned that the runner must do so according to rules and should strive lawfully (2 Cor. 2:5).

sections.title: The New Birth
sections.html:
The Bible teaches that being "born-again" is the only condition for entry into heaven. The "new birth" qualifies us to join the family of God, bringing us into the Kingdom of God's Son, Christ Jesus. It is through the new birth that we receive salvation by grace through faith (Ephesians 2:8-9).

The concept of a new birth is so crucially important for salvation that our Lord Jesus had to make it a special topic for His teaching.

The new birth is not only important for the very bad ones, the transgressors and sinners. It is also a must for the morally good, kind, and religious. "Church-goers" who are nominal christians must also receive the new birth if they have hope of ever seeing the Kingdom of God.

This is the reason our Lord told Nicodemus, "Verily, verily I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the Kingdom of God" (John 3:3). Nicodemus was a good man, very highly reputed man with a strong moral character. But Our Lord told him he must be born again.

The issue of being born again is not open-ended; it is not subject to exception or compromise. Our Lord left no room for differences of opinion on the matter. He said, "Ye must be born again". (John 3:7).

There is no exception as to sex, education, status in life, religious affiliation or denomination. Everyone who desires to see the Kingdom of God simply must be born again. A so-called christian who is not born again is as lost as an unbeliever who never accepted Christ as his Lord and Saviour.

This is because "in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature" (Galatians 6:15). For one to be a new creature is to be born again.

The Bible made it clear that "the heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?" (Jeremiah 17:9) and it is only God who can bring about a new birth by taking away "the stony heart out of the flesh, and will give back an heart of flesh" (Ezekiel 11:19).

Because man was conceived and born in sin (Psalm 51:5), Man therefore came short of the glory of God (Rom. 3:23) and this sinful condition requires a change, a new beginning, a new birth for the purpose of salvation.

The new birth which Christ demands is neither baptism nor reformation. A church may baptize someone to show that he is a christian. This is done by emersing him fully in water and bringing him up again as a sign that he has been "buried" with Christ, and then risen to a new life with the Lord.

Reformation means turning away from certain sinful ways or acts in one's life. This is not enough, because salvation requires a supernatural act of God.

What is required is a spiritual revolution, a complete turn-about so that the born again person is never the same again. A born again christian is a new creation, "old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new" (2 Cor. 5:17).

The first time we were born into this world it was a physical act but the second birth we are talking about is a spiritual act.

There are certain ingredients used in the new birth: There is the "Word of God" and there is also the "Spirit of God". James said that "of His own will begat He us with the Word of Truth" (James 1:18) while Peter said that, "being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of that, being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the Word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever" (1 Peter 1:23).

The central importance of the Word of God in the work of salvation is seen from the fact that faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the Word of God" (Rom. 10:17) and without faith it is impossible to please God (Hebrews 11:6).

As pertaining to the spirit of God, Christ Himself underscored its place in the regeneration process when he said emphatically, "Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the spirit, he cannot enter into the Kingdom of God" (John 3:5).

Christ added in verse 6 saying, "That which is born of the Spirit is spirit". It should be pointed out here that in reality no preacher or pastor ever converts anyone. The ministry of conversion is that of the Holy Spirit.

When the Word of God is preached to an unbeliever and he hears and receives the word, then the Holy Spirit first convicts him of his sins and thereafter the way is clear for the sinner's conversion.

Perhaps we should at this stage take note of the steps through which a sinner should pass in order to be born again. FIRST, a sinner or an unbeliever must express need to repent because everyone alive has already been proclaimed guilty in the sight of God (Rom. 3:10; Psalm 14:1-3).

Christ said, "Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish" (Luke 13:3). SECONDLY, repentance comes before believing. A person who is not repentant of his sins or who insists that he has committed no sins to repent of will have no basis to believe the gospel of Christ.

When Christ started His preaching ministry in Galilee He went about declaring that, "the time is fulfilled, and the Kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel" (Mark 1:14-15).

THIRDLY, repentance comes before forgiveness (Luke 24:47), and FOURTH, repentance comes before conversion as was seen in Peter's preaching when he said, "Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out..." (Acts 3:19). God said that "the time of ignorance He winked at: but now commandeth all men every where to repent" (Acts 17:30).

Conversion is the same as the new birth and we have just seen the steps by which a sinner can come to it. Then the next question is how to know that an unbeliever or a sinner has been born again. In trying to answer this question we should note that there is what we call"fruit of repentance".

A person who confesses that he is born again bu.. does not manifest the "fruit" is a liar. Christ said, "by their fruits ye shall know them" (Matt. 7:16 and 20) and in verse 21 He said that "Not everyone that said unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the Kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven".

If one loves the Lord he must keep His commandments (John 14:15).

sections.title: Evidence of the New Birth
sections.html:
There are several manifestations in the life of a born again person to show evidence of his new birth.

Evidence I: Righteous Living

One of such evidence of new birth is ability or power to live a righteous life. A born again person does not live a sinful life. "Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin" (1 John 3:9).

This verse does not mean that it is impossible for a born again christian to commit sin because he still has got his will and his mind. He can commit sin if he so desires, but if he does that, it means he has backsliden and forsaken God and must therefore be consumed along with transgressors and sinners (Isaiah 1:28).

Evidence II: Manifesting the "Fruit of the Spirit"

Another evidence in the life of a born again person is if he starts to manifest the fruit of the indwelling Holy Spirit in his daily life. Paul lists the fruit of the Spirit as: love, joy, peace, long suffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance (Galatians 5:22-23).

A person with the new birth has therefore received the Spirit of God in him and the evidence of it will be seen not only from how far and how deep he loves God but also whether he loves his neighbour as himself. This is the type of love Paul talked about in 1 Corinthians 13.

A born again person is always filled with joy; he has peace of mind, and "the peace of God which passeth all understanding" normally keeps his heart and mind through Christ Jesus (Philippians 4:7).

When you look at the new life of the new man you must see the above "fruit of the spirit" manifested, or else you know that his claim to new birth is counterfeit.

Evidence III: Attitude Towards The Bible

A further evidence will be in the attitude of the born again person toward the word of God, the Bible. When a person receives the new birth he acquires a new orientation or attitude towards the Bible. He learns to fear God and to place reliance on the word of God.

This is not difficult to understand because it was the Word of God which he heard and which changed his life as it has been said that "faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God" (Rom. 10:17).

God demands absolute obedience from His children and a born again child of God must endeavour to live by "every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God" (Matt. 4:4).

While a born again christian always accepts the word of God in the Bible as final authority, an unbeliever is always prepared for augument. Even many nominal christians today do not accept the Bible as the Word of God.

Some say that the different books of the Bible reflect the different views of their authors. Some of such church-goers have never read the Bible, while some who have read it do not believe that they should live by the promises and commandments of the Holy Book.

But this is pure ignorance because we are told in Acts 2:39 that the "promise (contained in the Bible) is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call".

God in these last days will not accept ignorance as an excuse for committing sin or for not worshipping Him as He deserves because we are already told in Acts 17:30 that "the times of this ignorance God winked at: but now commandeth all men everywhere to repent".

Obviously there are Christians who have zeal to worship God but who do so without knowledge of what God wants. Paul bore record of such people "that they have zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.

For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God" (Rom. 10:2-3).

Anybody with zeal but without knowledge may have the best of intentions but he will achieve no good result.

The goal sought may be correct but the way to accomplish it is wrong. It is like somebody who wants to go to London from Lagos but mistakingly he boards a plane for New York and he honestly believes he is flying to London.

The honesty of his belief will not save him or take him to London. He will be in New York instead.

There are many Christians today who would not read the Bible to know what God has said. They depend on church doctrines, traditions, formalities, and rituals even when these are not found in the Bible.

They contribute large sums of money to church building projects, attend committee meetings; they devote greater part of their time and money to church work thinking that salvation would come from such formalities. Such people have zeal without knowledge.

They have what someone called "blind zeal, unwise urgency and foolish purpose".

Having zeal but not according to knowledge is terrible because it "resists faith, opposes obedience to God's Word, and makes men stiff-necked and incorrigible".

Such people in their folly "insist upon their 'good intention' with stiff-necked and obstinate opposition, just as though they could not be mistaken; they believe that their salvation is altogether based upon the fact that they have good intentions and zeal of God.

Such people the Bible describes most properly as "perverse in heart and corrupt in mind".

The born again christian must see the author of the Bible as the Holy Spirit. We believe that God inspired not only the thoughts but also the words of the Bible.

The Holy Book is the only source of our knowledge of God; it is the textbook of divine truth; the guide book to everlasting life. Just as students read and inwardly digest their text books in order to pass their examination so must christians study the word of God, the Bible, to know the mind of God and what God requires from us.

It makes no sense for one to believe history books written about Alexander the Great, Homer, Plato and others we did not know personally but when it comes to the account of Jesus life and work there would be question, doubts, unbelief, double-mind, and so on. Why can't we give the same benefit of doubt to Bible account of our Lord Jesus as we give to history text books?

Paul, the Apostle, wrote Timothy telling him to "study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth" (2 Timothy 2:15). Obviously this admonition applies to all born again christians today.

Furthermore, Christians accept the Bible as the infallible Word of God. The Bible in this sense is the Canon of 66 Books. We do not recognize the Apocrypha or any other books to be inspired.

The christian Bible in our possession today will be used on the last day to judge the world. (John 12:48, Rev. 20:12), and therefore every living person who must surely face God on the judgment day must endeavour to read the Bible which is the basis upon which every one's trial, judgment, and sentence will be based. We must read it and obey it daily in our lives.

The people of God must handle this book carefully and reverently because it is God's Book "inspired by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness" (2 Tim. 3:16). Peter, the Apostle said, "Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the Scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost." (2 Peter 1:20-21).

You may take note of this fact. The Bible is known to have accurately predicted many historical events and it is only God who can do this. Examples include the following:

  • The re-establishment of the nation of Israel in 1948 (See Isaiah 11:11).

  • The destruction of the City of Tyre (Ezekiel 26).

  • The prediction of Daniel regarding the rise and fall of great Kingdoms (Daniel 2 and 7).

  • Various detailed predictions about the life, death, and resurrection of Christ: His birth place - Micah 5:2

  • The nature of His ministry - Isaiah 61:1-2

  • His scourging and crucifixion - Isaiah 53, Psalm 22:17, Zech. 12:10

  • His resurrection - Psalm 16:9-11.

Finally, it is believed that "the Bible has demonstrated itself to be God's inspired Word by its ability to transform individuals as well as reform society. In addition, the witness of countless thousands of believers point to the truth of the promises of God's Word.

The Bible's ability, through prophecy, to accurately predict future events also proves that it is God's Word".

Evidence IV: Witnessing

Another evidence that a person is born again or has received the new birth lies in his willingness, conviction, and courage to witness for Christ. Some people after their conversion try to live a secret disciple's life. They do not want to be identified as christian. They are ashamed that their friends will ridicule them as those "bible-carrying roadside-preachers".

Sometimes they may feel that they are still ignorant and do not know enough of the Gospel to preach to other people. While some are ashamed of what people will say about them, others are afraid they may lose their friends if they preach to them.

As a born again christian you are commanded by our Lord to confess Him openly to people. He said, "Whosoever therefore shall confess Me before men, him will I confess also before My Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny Me before men, him will I also deny before My Father which is in heaven" (Matt. 10:32-33).

If you do not confess Jesus Christ openly and publicly as your Lord and personal Saviour then you are a secret disciple like Nicodemus who the Bible said came to Jesus by night (John 3:2). He did not want to be seen publicly with Jesus; he did not want to be identified as a disciple of our Lord.

So also was Joseph Arimathaea who later openly confessed Christ when he asked to carry the body of our Lord (John 19:38).

For a christian who must live by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God, it is not possible to be a secret disciple without failing in our duties as commanded in Matt. 10:32-33 and Rom. 10:9. "For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation" (Rom. 10:10).

There are several advantages of our confessing Christ openly. We not only derive joy and blessings from it, but it also helps and strengthens us in our christian life. It gives us greater courage as it strengthens our faith in the Lord. Furthermore, witnessing for Christ ensures our stability in Christ; we are less likely to backslide provided we are not those who call Lord, Lord, and do not the things which He says (Luke 6:46).

By confessing Christ openly it helps to identify us with the Lord Himself and with other christians. Other people will get to know what we stand for and that our stand is not negotiable.

In so doing the unbelievers will not need to invite us to contribute to or participate in their funeral ceremonies, and to pay levy for masquerade, traditional dances, and age-grade meetings.

So it solves many social problems for christians to be identified openly as belonging to Christ so that no one will expect them to serve God and mammon at the same time.

A secret christian is a weak christian. He is cold, not hot and God has warned such people saying, "I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert (art) cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue (vomit) thee out of my mouth" (Rev. 3:15-16).

Remember that "It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God" (Heb. 10:31). Christ did a great and wonderful thing for us in dying for us so that we may live, and the least we can do for our Lord is to openly acknowledge His finished work of salvation on the Cross of Calvary.

Our courage and determination in witnessing and openly confessing our faith will surely win some more converts to Christ.

As a christian you are urged or even required to confess Christ publicly to friends, relatives, and even people you do not know.

You can just start off a conversation and ask if the person is a christian. If the answer is yes, find out if he is a born again Christian. If the answer is further yes, then praise the Lord and share your faith together.

But if he says he is just a "christian" and will not bother himself with whether he is born again or not, then in a most sympathetic way try to explain to him what being born again means and what Christ taught about it. Use John 3:3 as your take off point just as you would handle someone who is an unbeliever.

But remember St. Paul's advise that we should receive the weak in the faith "but not to doubtful disputations" (Rom. 14:1).

You should try to deal with such a christian with the greatest sympathy and understanding knowing that he is already on the broad road that leads to destruction.

You should try to get him to do about-turn and to submit himself to the Lordship of Jesus Christ and receive the new birth. Let the person know clearly that except a man be born again he cannot see the Kingdom of God, according to our Lord Jesus Christ in John 3:3.

Apart from confessing Christ to friends, relatives and neighbours in daily conversation, a christian should publicly confess our Lord in the Church gathering, in prayer meetings. A christian also confesses Christ by joining a true, spiritual, active christian church.

Some young converts often ask to know which is the right church to go to after conversion.

It is not advisable to recommend a church; the Holy Spirit will guide the new convert if he is sincere in his inquiry. The new spirit of God in him must be fed with the right type of spiritual food or else it will die, just like a newly born baby physically will die if it is not fed with the proper meal, or milk.

Therefore if his conversion is real, thorough, and complete, it is not likely that the old church in which he was a member before conversion can feed his new spirit and he must look for a new church.

Christ anticipated a situation like this when he said that, "no man putteth new wine into old bottle, else the new wine will burst the bottle and be spilled, and the bottle shall perish. But new wine must be put into new bottle, and both are preserved". (Matt. 9:17, Mark 2:22, Luke 5:38).

The new wine in this case is like the new spirit of the born again christian. The old bottle would be the former church he was attending before conversion. By trying to fit-in the new spirit into the old church there likely will be a burst, or a crisis, and either the church will drive the young convert away, or the new spirit will by itself find another church which is a true, spiritual, and active christian church for fellowship.

A person who is born again must be careful in choosing a church. What happens in most cases is that those people who say they are converted but remain in the same old church merely want to escape the pressures of friends and relatives by claiming conversion while in fact they remain on the road that is "broad", answering christian and still smoking, drinking, lying, cheating, fornicating and being involved in all vices that they can think of.

Such people should always remember that "wide is the gate and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction and many there be which go in thereat" (Matt. 7:13).

There are many of the so-called christians who always challenge you to show them where the Bible commands them not to drink (show them Leviticus 10:9), the Bible also tells us that it is sin to give any person wine to drink (Habakkuk 2:15).

The Bible too is against bribery and hypocrisy (Job 15:34). And some nominal christians are involved in all these sinful practices and still they hope to go to heaven.

Now to come back to our subject of witnessing, it is necessary that a confession of Christ is mainly to witness to the fact that one is a Christian. An unbeliever or a believer who lives in sin cannot be a faithful witness.

To be an effective witness, for example, in the court, you must know something; and such knowledge must be personal, not hearsay or imagination; it must be a positive and definite knowledge — a knowledge of something you heard, felt, tasted, touched or saw. Witnessing is not necessarily preaching sermons but telling simple truth or actual facts of life and work, ministry, death, resurrection, second coming, and last judgment of Christ as you know it.

The witness himself must be saved, so that under cross-examination, as in the law courts, his testimony will stand the test.

We said above that fear of men, and being ashamed of answering a born again christian are two factors that impede the witnessing and testimony of a new convert. Another factor is impure or sinful life.

If the newly converted person is still living in sin he will have no moral justification to preach to others to repent when he himself is still a sinner. Christ said that such a hypocrite should first cast out the "beam" out his own eye and then he will see clearly to pull out the "mote" that is in his brother's eye (Luke 6:42).

What the young convert should however do is not to stop witnessing because he has sinned. He should rather begin by confessing his sins according to 1 John 1:8-10, and by believing the promise of God in 1 John 2:1-2. That should restore him to God and restore confidence in himself to become an effective witness.

As a witness for Christ you should bear in mind what the Lord told us saying, "Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer, behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that you may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life" (Rev. 2:10).

In order to be further strengthened in your witnessing for Christ read the following passages carefully: Acts 4:13; 1 Peter 3:15-17; Titus 2:7-8; 1 Peter 2:11, 12, 15; 2 Tim. 2:12-13. Jesus said, "these things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer: I have overcome the world" (John 16:33).

The next evidence of the manifestation of the new birth to be considered is faith. Faith is about the most important factor in our relationship with God. Since God created us for His pleasure and to do His will (Philippians 2:13), a born again Christian must therefore endeavour to do everything to please God.

In order to discharge this important obligation christians must show faith in God because "without faith it is impossible to please Him: for he that cometh to God must believe that He is, and that He is a rewarder of them that diligently seek Him" (Heb. 11:6).

Faith in God means absolute reliance and trustful confidence in the Lord our Maker as in the case of a child who reposes all his confidence in the ability and willingness of his father to protect him in the face of an impending doom.

The challenging aspect of faith is the fact that christians are called upon to believe the evidence of things not seen, and to put our confidence in the substance of things hoped for (Heb. 11:1).
