No one has ever seen God but christians know (by faith) that God exists and this is what is meant when it is said that christians walk by faith not by sight (2 Cor. 5:7).

Faith is basic to Christian life because it is through faith alone that we are saved. "For by grace are ye saved through faith..." (Eph. 2:8). The word of God which we first heard and which the Holy Spirit used to convict us of our sins could not have been effective without faith because as we now know, faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God (Rom. 10:17).

By faith we believe the gospel and are saved. When Paul told the keeper of the prison at Philipi to "believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved and thy house" (Acts 16:31), he only asked the man to exercise his faith to believe the truth of the Word of God and it was the man's faith and the truth of the Word which brought him salvation and freedom. Freedom goes with Salvation because the truth which saves also makes one free. For "ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free" (John 8:32).

God is always looking at our faith and dealing with us according to the measure of it in us (Matt. 9:29). Therefore the stronger our faith is in Him the more intimately and the more profoundly He deals with us. The more we trust Him, believe Him, and rely on Him, the more satisfaction and benefits we get from our fellowship with Him. There are some examples to illustrate this point:

1. A Man sick of Palsy

When they brought to Jesus a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed, we are told that Jesus saw their faith and said unto the sick or the palsy: "Son be of good cheer: thy sins be forgiven thee" (Matt. 9:2, Mark 2:5).

Although the men carrying the sick person had love in them, but it was their faith that Jesus saw and healed the man and forgave him of his sins. The faith of the men brought healing to the sick.

2. The Centurion

The Centurion manifested a very strong faith in the healing power of our Lord asking Him not to bother to come to his house, but to speak the word only and his sick servant would be healed.

Christ first marvelled at the faith of the Centurion and then healed his servant telling him, "Go thy way; and as thou has believed, so be it done unto thee". The Bible said that the Centurion's servant was healed in the same hour. Note that the healing was performed only according to the faith of the Centurion (Matt. 8:8-10).

3. Blind Bartimaeus

The blind man, Bartimaeus, was tenacious in his faith. As Jesus was passing by, he had faith that the Lord Jesus could heal him and he started crying, "Thou Son of David, have mercy on me". He shouted very many times; each time the shouting got louder irrespective of every effort made by the crowd to silence him.

Christ asked him what he wanted and he replied "that I might received my sight". Then Jesus said unto him, "Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole" (Mark 10:51-52). Again it was the blind man's faith that healed him.

4. Daniel's Faith

Daniel showed remarkable and daring faith in defying King Darius' order or decree that no one in his Kingdom should worship any other god. Daniel's faith in the living God, the most High, saved him in the den of lions into which he was cast. (Daniel 6:10-23). It was Daniel's faith that saved him.

5. The Case of Job

Job was faced with a bleak future: his children had all died in a most terrifying circumstance; his wealth and property all destroyed, his wife had turned against him, friends all gone; the devil threatening him with death.

But in the face of all this adversity Job was not shaken in his faith in God. He said, "Though He slay me, yet will I trust in Him" (Job 13:15). "For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that He shall stand at the latter day upon the earth" (Job 19:25).

Job won the heart of God by his faith and was blessed with double blessings at the end.

6. The Syrophoenican Woman

The Syrophoenician woman also demonstrated a persevering faith as she engaged our Lord in a dialogue to get her daughter freed from devil possession.

She agreed with our Lord that children's bread should not be cast unto the dogs, but she also added that, "yet the dogs under the table eat of the children's crumbs". Jesus was obviously touched with such faith and He told her, "For this saying go thy way, the devil is gone out of thy daughter" (Mark 7:26-29).

Like the other cases above, it was this woman's faith in the Lord that healed her daughter.

7. The Heroes of Faith

We can also look at the long list of the Heroes of faith in Hebrews 11, and notice the special way God has always dealt with men of gigantic and unwavering faith, from Abel to Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Sara, Isaac, Joseph, Moses, and even Rahab, the harlot.

We can see that in each of the cases in which our Lord did a work of miracle there was first a believing heart. We notice that a great and unwavering trust was reposed on Him, and Jesus merely asked that they receive the healing they sought according to their faith.

A big faith will receive a big miracle; and small faith will receive a small miracle. This is one thing with faith: you reap as you sow. Faith therefore is confidence in God which leads us to believe the Word of God, the Bible.

It is by faith that we received Christ as our Lord and Saviour and confess Him to the world.

It is necessary to explain to the young convert that faith is not a blind act like asking one to jump in the dark. But rather faith in God rests securely upon the best available evidence which is the tried and tested infallible Word of God.

The only saving faith is that which casts itself on God either for life or for death. As Job said "even if He slay me yet will I trust Him".

In a situation of faith like this, Christ becomes all in all, and you begin to wish that Christ be magnified in your body, whether it be by your life or by death (Philippians 1:20); and that in all things Christ might have the pre-eminence (Col. 1:18). "He must increase but I must decrease" (John 3:30). This is a pure life of faith in Christ. "Christ in you, the hope of glory" (Col. 1:27).

We have seen that for a christian, faith is the gateway to receiving blessings from the Father. It is therefore important that we identify some sources of faith and clearly one of them is through the grace of God the Father working in us in which God "hath dealt to every man the measure of faith". this means that God has given to everyone a certain inward potential of faith.

Furthermore, it is given "to another faith by the same spirit" which also means that some people have more faith than others, for faith is one of the gifts of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 12:9).

Another source of faith is through the Son of God, Jesus Christ Himself. We are enjoined to "run with patience the race that is set before us, looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith..." (Heb. 12:1-2). The disciples of our Lord had asked Him to increase their faith (Luke 17:5) indicating clearly that Christ can give faith and can increase it. This He can do if we ask Him, for He has already told us saying

"What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them" (Mark 11:24). Certainly giving us faith and increasing it can be among the "things soever" we may desire and receive from our Lord just by asking.

Every christian has got faith and it grows and increases depending on how much we exercise it. It has been said already that "faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the Word of God".

This means that as we listen to the word of God preached, and as we read stories in the Bible our faith grows from strength to strength. In Acts 4:4 the people heard the word of God preached and they believed because of their faith in the Word. No one believes the Word of God who does not first have faith in God. Every Christian should be asked to pray with the man who confessed his faith saying, "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief" (Mark 9:24).

Lastly, the Holy Spirit is a source of faith as faith is listed as one of the "fruit of the Spirit" in Galatians 5:22. Note also that it is:

  • By faith we are saved. (Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto Him for righteousness (Rom. 4:3).

  • By faith we receive Christ — John 1:12

  • By faith we are justified — Rom. 5:1.

  • By faith we become children of God — Gal. 3:26

  • By faith we are sanctified — Acts 26:18.

  • By faith we are kept by the power of God — 1 Peter 1:5

  • Faith brings rest — Heb. 4:3.

  • Our heroes in Heb. 11 achieved everything they did because of their faith.

  • By faith we can be saved and spend eternity in heaven.

  • By lack of faith (unbelief) we will be cast in hell for ever and ever. (John 3:18)

Evidence VI: Holiness

We now come to the next evidence of the new birth or a born again spirit, and this is holiness or holy living. Holiness is similar to righteousness which we mentioned briefly before and which we shall go into more details now.

Holiness is a very important subject in the life of a christian because as we have seen earlier, God created man to have fellowship with Him and that is why man was created in the image of God after His likeness (Gen. 1:26).

Man in his original form was perfect, sinless, and holy until he was deceived by Satan to disobey God. The sin of disobedience caused the downfall of man and led to the punishment by death.

But by the grace and mercy of God, Christ was sent into this world and was sacrificed and made the propitiation for the sins of mankind (1 John 2:1-2) so that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish but have everlasting life (John 3:16).

Through Christ the fallen man is again restored to a state of perfection and holiness, but only to them who receive Jesus Christ in their life as the Lord and Saviour.

As Paul, the Apostle wrote, "Wherefore as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned... But not as the offence, so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ hath abound unto many" (Rom. 5:12-17).

Immediately after a person has received Christ and becomes a new creature, he is deemed to have been made holy by the holiness of Christ; he is sanctified, and he is made righteous before God.

The person is justified not by his own works or good deeds but by the grace of God in Christ Jesus. And because Christ now lives in us God commands us to be like Jesus, to live like Jesus, and in all things to be made perfect in Jesus.

Immediately God has delivered us out of the bondage of sin and Satan, He wants us to "serve Him without fear in holiness and righteousness all the days of our life" (Luke 1:74-75). Christ also commanded us saying, "Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect" (Matt. 5:48); He also said, "Be ye holy for I am holy" (1 Peter 1:16).

Although it is clear that God wants us to be holy and be perfect as He Himself is holy and perfect, but the devil in keeping with his ministry of lying, tells us otherwise. Many people today, even the so-called christians insist that it is impossible for anybody to be holy in this life.

Such people argue that God Himself knows that the world is evil and that no person in this evil world can say he is holy. According to them anybody claiming to be holy is like fish in the water claiming that it cannot be touched with water.

These people say that holiness, if it is ever possible, will be achieved in heaven not here on earth.

Again, man is seen here offering resistance to the Word of God. The Bible says that man shall live by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God (Matt 4:4). And God has said that we must "Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord" (Heb. 12:14).

Without holiness here and now we cannot see God after this life. This is what God said. But man rejects the Word of God and says he will first get to heaven and see God before he can become holy.

This is not possible. It is either we do it God's way, or we get ready to be cast into hell fire prepared for the devil and his angels (Matt 25:41).

I believe now that the choice is clear. It is either we choose to live as God requires us to live, that is, in holiness and righteousness all the days of our life (Luke 1:75), or we can continue to believe the lie of the devil and keep on living in our sins and unrighteousness and when we die we go to hell, a place of punishment (Matt. 25:46), a place of torment (Luke 16:23) or a place of fire (Rev. 14:10).

The Bible says that "The wicked shall be turned into hell, and all the nations that forget God" (Psalm 9:17). Having seen that heaven and earth shall pass away but the Word of God shall stand for ever (Matt 5:18), we must start to concern ourselves with holiness and what it means, and how we can begin to live that "holy, righteous, and sober life" today.

Holiness is the same as sanctification and we have seen that God commands it in our life now, not after. Sanctification is the will of God for every christian or believer. "For this is the will of God, even your sanctification" (1 Thess. 4:3). The Bible meaning of holiness or sanctification is separation, that is, to be set apart:

  • By God;

  • For God;

  • From Sin;

  • Unto a holy life (Psalm 4:3; Heb. 12:14; 2 Tim. 2:21).

It also means separation from evil (2 Chr. 29:15-18 also 2 Cor. 6:14-18) and separation unto God (Leviticus 27:16). Holiness is not achieved, one cannot work for it or earn it as a reward for something done for God.

Like Salvation, holiness is a free gift from God, and like every gift, holiness will be useless for anyone until it is received and applied in one's life.

There are several ways in which we are made holy or sanctified. First, we are made holy by the Word of God. Christ prayed to God, the Father, for the believers saying, "Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth" (John 17:17).

The Word of God purifies and cleanses and christians are urged to spend time in reading the Bible which is the Word of God. Some people make the mistake of saying that the Bible contains the Word of God. But note that the Bible is the Word of God.

Secondly, christians are made holy by the blood of Jesus even as Paul wrote, "Wherefore Jesus also, that He might sanctify the people with His own blood, suffered without the gate" (Heb. 13:12). The Word of God as the Light reveals the sin, and the blood of Jesus cleanses it away. "But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin" (1 John 1:7).

The third manner is by chastisement: "For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of His holiness... afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness" (Heb. 12:10-11). On the subject of chastisement see the following reference: Prov. 3:11-12; 1 Cor. 11:32-33; Heb. 12:5-6, 10-11).

The fourth way is by yielding ourselves completely to the direction of the Holy Spirit as we are commanded in Romans 6:19 to yield our members servants to righteousness unto holiness. Lastly, we can through our life, our actions, behaviour, thoughts, and the words we speak, bring about holiness in our lives. Paul wrote, "Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God" (11 Cor. 7:1).

Christians need not be afraid of the word holy, or of regarding themselves as holy people. Although any claim to holiness must be made reverently and in fear of God, yet the saints of God here on earth can claim holiness.

A life of holiness does not mean a life without sin. Christians are not people without sin but rather people whose sins are forgiven. Being a christian means learning to confess and forsake one's sins because we know that when we confess and forsake, God is faithful and just to forgive us and to cleanse us and make us holy (1 John 1:8-10).

If born again, spirit filled christians or believers cannot claim to be holy in this life who then can be saved? God has told us to "follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord" (Heb. 12:14).

If we therefore say that no person can be holy in this life then no one certainly shall see the Lord, and no one is now saved nor will ever be saved. Such a situation would defeat the whole purpose of God in sending His only Begotten Son Jesus Christ to die for the sins of the whole world so that man may through faith in Him be saved.

But we thank God that the grace of God cannot be made of none effect by the vile imaginations of man.

The Bible is clear on the matter: "These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God" (1 John 5:13).

In his Gospel account John wrote: "He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God" (John 3:18).

So we see from the Bible that he who hath Christ hath eternal life and he shall see God. And since only people who are holy in this life shall see God, it means therefore that those people who have Christ in this life, and who shall see God in the next life, are now holy people:

This agrees with the word of God, and christians should not allow the devil to deceive them or put fear into them: and rob them of their joy of salvation.

We are holy people if we have Christ in us because our righteousness is not of our own: it is Christ in us, the hope of glory.

We are made righteous through the righteousness of Christ: What we need to do on our part is to seek out the sin in our life, confess and judge it, cast it away, (that is, forsake it), pray to God to cleanse, purge, and purify us of the sin, and pray to God to give us strength and power to overcome the sin and thereafter to help us to live a life of Christ. We must claim, or appropriate Christ as our holiness on a daily basis.

We must daily claim His holiness, His faith, His love, His grace. Holiness in this life is nothing other than this continuous appropriation of our Lord's holy life day by day.

The more we claim His holiness the more we are able to live that holy, righteous and sober life. We cannot be holy by our own effort but God is able and faithful to bring us to such perfection because "faithful is He that called you, who also will DO IT" (1 Thess. 5:24).

The next and perhaps last evidence of the new birth we can discuss in this study is works of faith.

Some Christians make the mistake of stopping with salvation. When once they call upon the Lord, confessing Him with their mouth, and believing in their heart that God raised Him from the dead and receiving the new birth which is salvation, then such people start behaving as if salvation is the end of the road for the born again christians

Christians should note that by their salvation they are called unto good works. It is true that it is by grace we are saved through faith and not by works (Eph. 2:8), but the Apostle James has said too that faith without good works is dead (James 2:17, 20).

This point should be made clear from the outset. There are unbelievers who quote this verse in James 2:20 that "faith without works is dead" and they therefore rely solely on their so-called good works like giving alms to the poor, and feel that they will receive salvation by such works.

The Bible says that it is "by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast" (Eph. 2:8). Furthermore, those who trust in their good works to earn them salvation and justification before God are reminded in Isaiah 64:6 that "all our righteousness are as filthy rags" before God.

It is only after we have accepted Jesus Christ as our Lord and personal Saviour and are assured of salvation can we start to show our faith by good works.

Just as it is a mistake for people who are not first saved to rely on good works, so it is a mistake for christians who are assured of salvation to neglect doing works of faith.

A born again christian who has no works will receive no reward from God on the Day of Judgment and he will be saved as by fire, which means that he would be saved but just narrowly. So although the just shall live by faith (Gal 3:11) yet we are commanded after our new birth to "work out our salvation with fear and trembling, For it is God which worked in us both to will and to do His good pleasure" (Phil. 2:12, 13).

What is to be remembered is that after our conversion we are called to do good works because we are saved already, not in order that we might be saved.

The born again christians who say that they have faith and that works are not necessary in christian living should read James chapter 2:14-26 written for christians. Can faith alone save?

The answer is 'no' because "faith if it hath not works, is dead being alone" (verse 17-18, 20-26).

James is not referring to initial justifying faith, but to the demonstration of christian faith before men, even as the Lord commanded us saying, "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father which is in heaven" Matt. 5:16 see also Matt. 16:27, Eph. 2:10, 1 Tim. 6:18, 2 Tim. 3:17, Titus 1:16).

No person is justified by works (Rom. 3:25-31; 4:1-6; 9:11; 11:6, Gal. 2:16, Eph. 2:8-9, Titus 3:5) but persons already justified and saved must do works to prove their christian calling and consecration (James 2:14-18, 20-26).

Just as faith without works is dead, so are works without faith dead. Neither of them is complete in itself. Even believing in God is no proof that one is justified by faith, for even devils believe and tremble without justification (James 2:19).

We can therefore see that faith is good because without faith it is impossible to please God (Heb. 11:6). But we should not stop there because faith is not sufficient in itself, and this is the reason the Bible says that we must "add to faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; and to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; and to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness love" (2 Peter 1: 5-7).

And similarly, James wrote that "faith, if it hath not works, is dead being alone" (James 2:17).

The Bible has given us examples of good works with which Christians should concern themselves:

  • Glorification of God: "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Matt. 5:16, Col. 1:10).

  • Enrichment of Life: "That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate" (1 Tim. 6:18).

  • Furnishing a Pattern for Imitation: "In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity" (Titus 2:7; 2:14; 3:8).

  • Summoning others to their task: "And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works" (Heb. 10:24).

  • Demonstrating the reality of faith: "Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone" (James 2:17).

  • Yea, a man may say, Thou hath faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works" (James 2:18).

  • Having your conversation honest among the Gentiles (unbelievers), that whereas they speak against you as evil doers, they may by your good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation" (1 Peter 2:12).

  • Other examples of good works:

  • For I was an hungered, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in" (Matt 25:35).

  • Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me" (Matt 25:36).

  • There came unto him a woman having an alabaster box of very precious ointment, and poured it on his head, as he sat at meat. But when his disciples saw it, they had indignation, saying, To what purpose is this waste? When Jesus understood it, he said unto them, Why trouble ye the woman? for she hath wrought a good work upon me" (Matt. 26:7).

  • Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and alms-deeds which she did" (Acts 9:36).

  • Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love, and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, in the sight of God and our Father" (1 Thess. 1:3).

  • I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience; and how thou canst not bear them which are evil: and thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars" (Rev. 2:2).

Let us also consider the effect of good works done before the new birth and which cannot earn salvation. The works are as filthy rags before God. They include the following examples:

  • Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devil? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then I will profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity" (Matt. 7:22-23).

People to be warned here include Pastors, Ministers, Evangelists, Bishops, and Archbishops, and all other church hierarchies who work in many churches today but who are not born again christians.

God will not prevent these so-called "Servants of God" from preaching the gospel with even signs and wonders, following their work. God said, "I will hasten my Word to perform it" (Jeremiah 1:12).

Any preaching and healing done in the Lord's name will be honoured by God. However, if the preacher or a miracle worker is not a born again christian, he shall still be cast into the hell fire at the end, because our Lord was clear on the point when he said "Except a man be born again, he cannot see the Kingdom of God" (John 3:3).

Paul said "I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means when I have preached to others, I myself should be a cast-away" (1 Cor. 9:27).

Paul here is not afraid of his salvation, however, every saved person must worry about his good works and rewards.

I have used this Paul's case as example that even preachers and all servants of God must first make sure they are saved before doing good works else the good works will not count for anything: neither for salvation nor for reward.

Our Lord will surely tell them on the last day: "depart from me, ye that work iniquity, I never knew you".

May all who say they work for God today take heed of this warning and know that God will not take His Word to accommodate their disobedience and convenience.

Let them also remember that "God is no respecter of persons" (Acts 10:34) and what God says He will do He will surely do it.

  • Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin" (Rom. 3:20; 9:32; 11:6).

  • Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified" (Galatians 2:16).

  • For by grace are ye saved through faith, and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast" (Eph. 2:8-9, 2 Tim. 1:9).

  • Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost" (Titus 3:4).

Born again, saved Christians, are specially commanded to do good:

  • To "depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it" (Psalm 34:14).

  • To "trust in the Lord, and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed" (Psalm 37:3, 27).

  • To "love your enemies, and do good; and lend hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil" (Luke 6:35; Rom. 13:3; Gal 6:10; 1 Tim. 6:18).

  • To do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased" (Heb. 13:16).

  • Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin" (James 4:17, 1 Peter 2:15, 3:11, 17).

sections.title: How to Receive Salvation
sections.html:
Having gone through these seven evidences and manifestations of the new birth, I want to make it clear that salvation, although it is free, must be received before it starts to manifest in ones life.

Let us take for example the case of a man who was convicted of murder by our Supreme Court and was kept in jail while his application for State pardon was being considered by the President and the Head of State.

Subsequently the man's application was approved and the President wrote him telling him that he had been granted pardon, and he would no longer be executed if he accepted the pardon.

The convicted man received the President's letter, looked at it, and for some unexplained reasons he tore the letter of pardon into pieces and threw it away into a waste paper basket.

This action was reported to the Supreme Court which met and decided that since the man tore the letter as a sign that he rejected the pardon, the law had no alternative than to go ahead with the order for execution of judgment.

The man thereafter was hanged on the neck till he died.

It should be noted that this man committed the crime, he was properly found guilty; he was given a pardon which would have saved his life but he rejected it.

This is the same situation in which many people find themselves today. The pardon for our sins was given by God in the person of Jesus.

If we fail to receive Jesus as our Lord and personal Saviour, His sacrifice on the Cross of Calvary is made in vain in our lives, and we shall die eternally.

One does not get saved because one attends a church. In fact somebody can attend the church all his life without getting saved. He may follow others to sing, praise God, pray, and go for soul-winning and yet he himself is not saved.

Salvation comes with being born again; there must be a new birth. For a new birth to take place one must admit before God that he is a sinner and that he cannot save himself.

He must repent of all the sins in his life, confess them before God, and make a conscious decision to forsake them, that is, never to go back to those sins. He will then ask Christ to come into him and make his heart His abode.

At this stage the person has come to God, provided he has done so in sincerity and in truth. God's response is immediate and certain for He has promised saying, "him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out" (John 6:37).

There must be a conscious decision on the part of the unbeliever or a nominal christian to receive Jesus and enter into the new birth. Some church-goers say that they were born into a christian family and therefore they have been christians since their birth.

There is nothing like inheriting the new birth, or to say that because your parents are christians therefore you have become a christian by birth.

Everybody must decide for himself whether to follow Jesus or to follow the devil. Your father, mother, brother, sister, son, daughter, husband, wife, or friend cannot make the decision for you.

Some people say that the evidence that they are saved is the baptism by which water was sprinkled on their head and then later they were confirmed and they started to receive the Holy Communion.

All these things are not bad, but they cannot make anyone a christian nor can they bring salvation to any person. The only thing that can save anyone is the new birth.

The key to the new birth is shown by the Apostle Peter after his sermon on the day of Pentecost: "Now when they heard this, they were pricked in their heart, and said unto Peter and to the rest of the apostles, MEN AND BRETHREN, WHAT SHALL WE DO? Then Peter said unto them, REPENT, AND BE BAPTISED every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost" (Acts 2:37-38 see also 2:21 and 3:19).

This passage shows that a person who seeks the new birth must first hear the gospel since "faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the Word of God" (Rom. 10:17).

Peter preached the gospel of Christ in power on the day of Pentecost and people's hearts were pricked (or the Holy Ghost convicted them of their sins) and they sincerely inquired to know what to do to be saved.

Similarly, whoever wants to be saved today must inquire as to what he could do and any child of God will be readily available to lead him to Christ. When you seek salvation sincerely and with all your heart you must be pricked at heart.

You must shed tears for the years of rebellion and disobedience against God. I have not yet seen any person who repented and got saved who did not shed tears. God said that a broken and contrite heart He will not despise (Psalm 51:17).

After the tears and the salvation which follows, the person would never be the same again.

Salvation brings revolution to someone's life not amendment or renovation. It is a total change, "old things are passed away and behold all things are become new" (2 Cor. 5:17).

If all who knew you before did not notice that you are now a new creature, then you are not yet born again. After the heart is pricked, sins are confessed, and one repents of them.

Peter told them to "Repent and be Baptised". Baptism never goes before repentance. But in our traditional churches today even children of three months old are baptised. How could any person expect a baby to repent - repent of what?

Many people today who are "christians" and who hope to go to heaven went through the infant baptism. And they still hope to see the Kingdom of God when they are not yet born again (John 3:3).

Where is the Bible authority for their infant baptism and for expecting to see the Kingdom of God without the new birth?

When Christ came in contact with the little children in the Bible it was not for baptism but for blessing. "And they brought young children to him, that he should touch them: and his disciples rebuked those that brought them.

But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them, "suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not for of such is the Kingdom of God. Verily I say unto you,

Whosoever shall not receive the Kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein. And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them" (Mark 10:13-16).

It is very clear from the authority of the Bible that baptism should not be given to the infants but rather to adults only after they had repented and been converted.

Without repentance there can be no remission of sins. And we cannot today repent and tomorrow we go back into the same sin.

We must repent and forsake the sin, and then God would be found faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness (1 John 1:9).

It is only when we have followed the steps outlined in the Bible in seeking God shall we find Him.

Similarly, if we seek Salvation and the new birth which alone guarantee us entry into the Kingdom of God we must be prepared to follow the Bible teaching on it.

We must refuse to allow man's wisdom, devices, and the lies of the devil to shipwreck us out of God's plan which He made for our salvation before the foundation of the earth.

sections.title: The Judgment
sections.html:
The next most important event the whole world must witness any time from now is the Second Coming of our Lord Jesus.

This Second coming will mark the end of this present World Age and mark the beginning of the Kingdom of God here on earth in which Christ shall rule and reign with His Saints for 1,000 years, generally called the Millennium.

But before this period starts God must first settle some scores with men whom He created and allowed to inhabit the face of the earth. God will judge every one both living and dead to determine which souls of men qualify to continue their existence in the Millennial Kingdom.

Because God is just and righteous, He said he will judge the whole world in righteousness and in equity. "For he cometh, for he cometh to judge the earth: he shall judge the world with righteousness, and the people with his truth" (Psalm 96:13).

God created man and made him a free moral agent allowing him to choose to worship God, the Creator, or to worship the devil or gods made with hands (Psalm 115:4-8).

God gave man that free-will of choice, either to choose to do good and go to heaven, or to do evil and go to hell. God said to man, "Behold, I set before you this day a blessing and a curse: A blessing, if ye obey the commandments of the Lord your God. . . And a curse, if ye will not obey the commandments of the Lord your God" (Deut. 11:26-28).

It has never been in the plan of God to force man to worship Him. There are people today who complain saying "If God be Lord why does He allow evil in the world" . . . Why does God allow the devil or the Satan to deceive man and spoil God's creation?"

But God's plan did not include compelling man to fear Him and to keep His commandments. If God had forced and compelled man to worship Him, to fear Him, and keep His commandments, you would also hear people complain that God is a tyrant; that He created us and refused to allow us any freedom or free-will to do whatever we choose to do.

We will call Him a wicked person. But God in His infinite wisdom and knowledge allowed us a free-hand; and men rather than choose to know his Creator, chose to obey and worship the enemy of God, the devil.

But God decided that because man has the right to choose what he wants to do.

He, God, will have right also to judge man according to what he has done whether it be good or evil, "For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ: that everyone may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad" (2 Cor. 5:10).

Nothing that a man has done will ever escape the judgment of God. Even the secrets of men will be subjected to scrutiny and judgment, "In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to the gospel" (Rom. 2:16).

But in spite of these expressly clear statements of God on the subject of the Last Day of Judgment, people today still argue whether infact God has spoken. The lie and deceit which the devil started with Adam and Eve about 6,000 years ago he has continued with the people of today and he continues winning many supporters to his side.

These devil's supporters oppose the Word of God and contend that the Books of the Bible are the personal views and philosophy of the writers. They do not believe that the Bible is the Word of God. They deny the existence of God and say that there is nobody like the "Son of God".

But God said that "if we deny him he also will deny us: If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself" (2 Tim. 2:12-13).

Therefore the fact that man says there will be no Judgment of God makes no difference: the Word of God abideth forever and what God said He will do He will surely do it. So there must be accountability.

Man must face his maker and give account of what he has done in his body whether it be good or bad. This is the plan of God for mankind (Rom. 14:12).

Although there are many types of judgment described in the Bible, we shall only be concerned in this book with only two most important ones: First is the judgment of believers at the Judgment Seat of Christ, called the “Bema (2 Cor. 5:10) and secondly, the judgement of the unbelievers when they shall appear before the Great White Throne (Rev. 20:11-15).

So we shall take up first judgement at the judgement Seat of Christ.

sections.title: Judgment of the Believers
sections.html:
We now know from the Scriptures that the judgment of the believers at the Judgment Seat of Christ shall take place soon after our Lord Jesus Himself appears in the clouds.

This appearance will mark the end of this world in the present form and another world Age, which is the Kingdom Age, or the Kingdom of Christ, which will last for 1,000 years, would be ushered in.

This is Paul's description of these coming events: "For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God; and the dead in Christ shall rise first; Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord" (1 Thess. 4:16-17).

All who believe in Christ, lived holy life, and died in the Lord shall resurrect and meet Jesus in the air; and after them, almost at the same time, those who are alive and remain in the Lord, who live a holy, righteous and sober life, shall be changed in a twinkle of any eye and shall all fly off to meet with our Lord in the air.

There will surely be utter confusion on that day as the Lord selects His own children to meet Him while leaving behind the devil and his agents to bemoan their fate. Jesus Himself gave us some insight into how the whole thing would look like.

He said, "I tell you, in that night there shall be two men in one bed: the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left. Two women shall be grinding together: the one shall be taken and the other left. Two men shall be in the field: the one shall be taken, and the other left" (Luke 17:34-36).

Our Lord's reference to "night" here may suggest that the end may come at night. But He also suggests it might be by day time when men are still working in the field. However, nobody actually knows the time.

Our Lord said, "But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father" (Mark 13:32, Also Acts 1:7).

Then after all the saints and the holy children of God had been gathered in the air they will remain with the Lord for ever. For the first few years (some say 3½ years) while they are with the Lord, most probably in heaven, the earth will be witnessing some great events too.

The Anti-Christ will be revealed and he will promise peace if everyone will accept his bid to rule the whole world. So there will be a period of false peace in the world for those few years.

Then in the second period (which some also say is 3½ years) the Anti-Christ will reveal his real identity and would start a pogrom against those who refuse to worship him as god, and those who call on the name of Jesus as their Lord and Saviour.

A great tribulation such that the world never knew, nor shall ever know, will start. The Jews would be greatly persecuted and just before the Anti-Christ and his world army would wipe them off from the face of the earth, the Lord Jesus will descend to earth to rescue a remnant of the Jews, about 144,000 of them.

This would mark the second coming of our Lord on this earth (Rev. 7:4-8; 12:6, 14).

During the period the Saints are with the Lord, two great events would be going on at the same time as the other great events would be taking place on the earth.

There would be judgment of the believers at the Judgment Seat of Christ (Matt. 16:27; Rom. 14:10; 2 Cor. 5:10; Rev. 22:12). And there would also be the Marriage Supper or Marriage Feast of the Lamb (Rev. 19:7-9).

Jesus Christ our Lord will be the Bridegroom while His Bride would include all Christians who have trusted and believed in Christ during the Age of Grace or the Church Age, starting from the Day of Pentecost till the time our Lord appeared in the air (Matt. 22:1-4; 2 Cor. 11:2, Eph. 5:32).

But what concerns us here is not the Marriage Feast but rather the Judgment Seat of Christ.

The judgment of believers at the Judgment Seat of Christ will not be a trial to decide whether a person is saved or not saved. Any person who appears at this judgment is already saved and he must have taken part in the First Resurrection of those who met the Lord in the air.

The question of salvation will be a settled thing in this life only. After we are saved, the Lord commands us to do good as we have already discussed above, and James the Apostle brought the point nearer home in his writing that "faith without works is dead" (James 2:20).

Therefore during this judgment the believer will be judged for his works based on 2 Cor. 5:10 "For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that everyone may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad".

The manner of this judgment was described by our Lord in His illustration of the Kingdom of Heaven in Matt. 25:14-30. The Lord at this time of His return to earth shall examine each of us in the use we made of the one, two, or five talents He had entrusted to our care.

Everyone must give account of every opportunity or responsibility God gave him in this life as to how he used them, good or bad.

There will be no judgment of any person's sins which he committed before conversion because God promised saying, "And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more" (Heb. 10:17).

Furthermore, the sins the believer committed and confessed after conversion will not be judged. The sins of the Saints are all wiped away and hidden underneath the blood of Christ. They were all forgiven by God as he promised in 1 John 1:8-10.

So the things to be judged at the Judgment Seat of Christ are:

● OUR WORKS: "Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is" (1 Cor. 3:13). Also "For God shall bring every work into judgment with every secret thing, whether it be good or whether it be evil" (Eccles. 12:14).

● OUR WORDS: Our Lord said that, "every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment. . . for by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned" (Matt. 12:36-37). However, if one is condemned by one's words one would then appear at the Great White Throne Judgment not at the Judgment Seat of Christ.

● OUR THOUGHTS: Even the thoughts we hold in our mind or in our heart, if they are evil, will be judged, "For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies; These are the things which defile a man" (Matt. 15:18-20).

Furthermore, our Lord commanded us saying, "whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart" (Matt. 5:28).

But a Christian who sinned in this manner but confessed them according to 1 John 1:9 will not come into judgment. However, if such sins are not confessed, the sinner, whether a christian or not, would end up in hell and would never appear at the Judgment Seat of Christ.

● OUR SECRETS: Paul wrote that we should not judge anything before the Last Day Judgment, until our Lord will come "who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the heart" (1 Cor. 4:5).

All the secret sins and evil thoughts buried in our hearts which we thought could never see the light of day will be revealed and manifested at the Judgment.

Again, the only hope for a christian is if such secret sins are confessed and forsaken, else they would lead the sinner to the Great White Throne Judgment, not to the Judgment Seat of Christ.

● OUR MOTIVES: The hidden counsels of the heart which will be judged include bad motives which alone are known to God.

On that day many of the good christian works people did would be thrown away because of the hidden bad motives with which the works were done. For example, a christian work done by somebody who harbours impure, angry, or revengeful thoughts in his heart will not count or be rewarded.

That is why our Lord said, "If thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee; Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift" (Matt. 5:23-24).

At the judgment, the evil thoughts or bad motives will be revealed to destroy the otherwise good works the person has done.

Furthermore, doing good works not as to the Lord (Col. 3:17, 23) but as to men to obtain praise and glory mwill not do. "Therefore let no man glory in men" (1 Cor. 3:21).

Christ warned us saying, "Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven" (Matt. 6:1). But rather christians are urged to "run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking Unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith" (Heb. 12:1-2).

● OUR UNCONFESSED SINS: We are told in 1 John 1:8-9 never to say that we have no sin, but that we should rather confess our sins and God is faithful and just to forgive us our sins. "If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us" (verse 10).

It warms our heart to know that any confessed sin is completely forgotten and forgiven by God and will be "remembered against us no more". However, if we refuse, or neglect or forget, to confess and to forsake any sin in our life God will then see us as sinners to be condemned equally with unbelievers or transgressors according to Isaiah 1:28.

So you can note that unconfessed sin will deny a born again christian a place at the Judgment Seat of Christ and all the works he did and the rewards he thought he got would never be mentioned. He will instead spend eternity in hell fire for simply failing to confess and forsake his sins.

Remember always that God is not deceived, nor is He mocked: "For whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap" (Gal. 6:7-8).

The result of the whole judgment exercise is that the works which are burned by fire will mean loss for the individual, but works that remain after the burning shall be rewarded as good.

Thus, "if any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire" (1 Cor. 3:15). It is not disclosed in the Bible what the loss will be but we are told that a reward shall be a crown. So it is likely that the loss of a reward or crown will bring shame.

Christians are called upon to produce good works for their reward in heaven. Our Lord commanded us saying, "Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also" (Matt. 6:19-20).

Now there are two types of building materials the Bible talked about in 1 Cor. 3:12. One type is fire-proof and it consists of gold, silver and precious stones; the other type is combustible and consists of wood, hay and stubble. Those works which cannot burn (the fireproof) are:

● RIGHTEOUSNESS, which is a clean and pure life before God. Yet the righteousness is not of our own for we are rather clothed with the righteousness of Christ so that it is Christ in us the hope of glory (Col. 1:27).

● HONESTY, not only before men but also before God. (1 Tim. 2:2).

● LIFE OF FAITH, faith in God, faith in Christ, faith in the Word of God (the Bible), see Hebrews 11.

● LOVE, this must be true love, the type Paul talked about in 1 Cor 13; love towards God and towards man. The Lord commanded, saying, "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: This is the first commandment. And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself" (Mark 12:30-31).

● PATIENCE, this is a highly rated virtue. Paul admonished Timothy saying, "But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness" (1 Tim. 6:11).

● MEEKNESS AND HUMILITY, Meekness is one of the fruits of the Spirit (Gal. 5:23). Our Lord said, "come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart; and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light" (Matt. 11:28-30).

● PEACEFUL. "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God" (Matt. 5:9). We are commanded in 2 Tim. 2:22 "... to follow... peace with men that call on the Lord out of a pure heart" and in Hebrews 12:14 we are asked to "follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord".

The works represented by materials that can burn (the combustible) include the works of unrighteousness for which the doers of such works would spend their eternity in hell fire. Such works are:

● CHEATING AND BRIBERY: God said that "the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacle of bribery. For they conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit" (Job 15:34-35).

● DISHONESTY: All works done in dishonesty shall be burned, particularly in the Ministry, and in the handling of the Word of God, if done deceitfully and in dishonesty.

We are commanded: "Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth" (2 Tim. 2:15). Therefore, when one has received this Ministry and have also received mercy, he must renounce "the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling of the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God" (2 Cor. 4:1-2).

This warning must specially go to the pastors and preachers of the Word of God who at times speak not to edify the Church but who use the pulpit to pursue personal vendetta against individuals or groups in the church.

God knows the mind and the motives of such preachers or teachers and if their work is good but the motive is bad and evil, there will be no reward because the work shall be burned and they will suffer shame on the Day of Judgment.

● BENEFITS derived through undue influence shall not escape the burning flames of the fire of judgment.

● YIELDING TO YOUTHFUL LUSTS. Paul warned in his letter to Timothy that "they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts which drown men in destruction and perdition.

For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted and pierced themselves through with many sorrows. But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness" (1 Tim. 6:9-11; See also 2 Tim. 2:2 and Joseph in Genesis 39:12).

● GOOD THINGS done with wrong or evil motives, for example one gives alms in order to seek ones glory or praise (Matt. 6:1-4).

● PRIDE is a great sin before God, and He said He will scatter the proud in the imagination of their hearts (Luke 1:51).

The sin of Lucifer, the leader of the Angelic hosts, for which God punished him with everlasting damnation is the sin of pride. "For thou has said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north. I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High" (Isaiah 14:10-18).

Any works done with pride shall be burned. However, the sin of pride would have to send the christian not to the Judgment Seat of Christ, but to the Great White Throne Judgment. Pride is sin and it must be avoided, or confessed, when we are over-come by it.

The reward which believers shall receive for good works not burned are represented by crowns, and there are five of them, namely:

● The Crown of Righteousness;

● The Crown of Life;

● Crown of Rejoicing;

● The Crown of Glory;

● The Incorruptible Crown.

● The Crown of Righteousness.

This crown will be won by those who lived a very holy and righteous life only because of the love they have for Christ and His imminent Second Coming.

These overcomers lived by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God (Matt. 4:4). They feared God and kept His commandments. They kept their life shining so that men could see their good works and glorify our Father in Heaven. The Crown is revealed in 2 Timothy 4:8: "Finally, there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will give me on that Day; and not to me only but also to all who have loved His appearing" Every christian ought to covet this Crown.

It requires watching and praying for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ because no one knows the day, or the hour or even the season (Mark 13:32, Acts 1:7).

● The Crown of Life

This is often described as the Crown for faithful ones and it is revealed in James 1:22. "Blessed is the man who endures temptation; for when he has been proved he will receive the crown of life which the Lord has promised to those who love Him"

The Crown is sometimes called the "martyr's crown" or the sufferer's crown and it will have the effect of redressing many of the injustices christians suffered in this life. There appears to be three conditions for winning this crown:

● enduring temptation and overcoming evil,

● loving the Lord, and

● being faithful unto death, which means not only enduring till the end of ones life on earth, but even giving ones life to martyrdom, to be killed for the sake of the gospel of Christ.

Rev. 2:10 says, "Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life".

In Philippians 1:20 we are also commanded that "Christ shall be magnified in our body, whether it be by life, or by death". That means that we must be prepared to have Christ magnified and glorified in our body even if we have to suffer persecution and die as a result.

This is the way this crown can be won by a christian. Many before us like Stephen, Peter, and Paul in the Bible have already won this crown, and we are sure that many more today will also win it. It only requires special grace of God because as Christ said "Without me ye can do nothing (John 15:5).

● The Crown of Rejoicing

This is often called Crown for soul winners and it is reserved for those who took it as their first duty to win lost souls to Christ. It is not for those who win souls by accident but rather for those who gave themselves over as their primary responsibility to win the souls of the unbelievers.

Those who preach to the already converted souls build on another person's foundation and they will receive no crown. This crown is revealed in 1 Thess. 2:9, "For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Are not even ye in the presence of the Lord Jesus Christ at His coming?"

The Crown will represent the total number of converts we got for Christ and each convert may likely represent a jewel on that Crown. So one can begin to calculate the number of jewels one will get on one's Crown on that Day.

But there should be a note of warning here. We do not convert any person. It is the work of the Holy Spirit to convict and to convert a sinner to the Lord (John 16:8-11). We are merely commanded to teach and preach the Word of God and it is God Himself who gives the increase (Matt 28:19).

It is not every person who repented following our preaching that will give us a jewel on the Crown. For example, if 50 people repented through our ministry and 30 fell away from the faith before they die, we shall be left with only 20 jewels on our Crown. It will be unjust for you to expect 50 jewels if only 20 of your converts finally make it to Heaven.

This is why it is important that we do not only aspire to win souls but we must also try to tender the souls we have won. For example, Paul went back three times in his missionary journeys to try to consolidate the souls he won. We must be our brother's keeper to be able to retain the number of souls we have won for Christ.

● The Crown of Glory

This is also known as Crowns for true pastors, the "Shepherd's crown" which is given to those who dedicated their lives to the teaching and preaching of the Word of God.

It is a crown for the elders, the shepherds, the pastors, teachers, evangelists, missionaries, and other servants of God such as faithful Sunday School teachers.

Although the number entrusted to a sunday school teacher is small but he still is "feeding the flock" with the Word of God. And if a sunday school teacher, or house-to-house fellowship teacher is "faithful in a few things" he will be made a "ruler over many" (Matt. 25:23).

This Crown is revealed in 1 Peter 5:1, 4: "The elders who are among you I exhort, I who am a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a partaker of the glory that will be revealed: and when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that does not fade away".

● The Incorruptible Crown

This is often called the "victor's crown" or crown for runners. It is revealed in 1 Cor. 9:24-27 "Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain. And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things.

Now they do it to obtain corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible. Therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air. But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be cast away"

This crown can only go to a christian who is prepared to pay the price or "to go the extra mile" (Matt. 5:41). It is required that the body or the flesh which is very unruly should be "kept under" and brought "into subjection".

To win this crown our bodies must be constantly purged, purified, cleansed and sanctified and must be presented "a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is our reasonable service" (Rom. 12:1).

Christians must be prepared to "run with patience the race that is set before us, looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith" (Heb. 12:1-2).

We must bear in mind that what counts is not how well we started the race but how well we are continuing it, and how well we shall end it.

Lastly, if we can only persevere in our longing and expectation of our Lord's imminent return to earth, not only shall we be comforted (1 Thess. 4:18) but we shall also be laying up for ourselves a crown of righteousness which is available for those "who have loved His appearing" (2 Tim. 4:8).

A Christian can have as many as all the five Crowns. May the Lord be your strength and your shield. Amen.\

sections.title: Judgment of the Unbelievers
sections.html:
In this part of the Judgment we shall be concerned with the fate of the unbelievers who die in their sins before the Second Coming of our Lord.

As we have seen already, the believers will be judged for their works at the judgment Seat of Christ (2 Cor. 5:10); but the unbelievers will appear before the Lord at the Great White Throne Judgment (Rev. 20:11-15).

The time for the White Throne Judgment is located at the end of the Millennial rule, or the 1,000 years of the Kingdom of Christ here on earth. For example, an unbeliever who dies today shall immediately go to hell and will remain there from now till Christ comes, and he will also be in hell throughout the 1,000 years when Christ and His Saints shall rule and reign in the millennial Kingdom.

On the other hand, if a believer dies today, his soul goes immediately to heaven, which used to be Paradise; this is a resting place for the saved souls before the judgment.

From this resting place he will then meet Christ in the air for the Final Judgment and the Marriage Feast, and then down to earth to rule and reign with Christ for 1,000 years (Rev. 20:4-5).

So we can see the difference in the position of an unbeliever and a believer. If Christ were to come again this year, a believer who died just before, will rise up at once and be with the Lord while an unbeliever who died at the same time will remain in hell for the next 1,000 years during which Christ and His Saints will rule the earth.

Then at the end of the 1,000 years the unbeliever will be resurrected for judgment at the White Throne Judgment.

So the resurrection of a believer will be immediately Christ appears in the clouds (1 Thess. 4:17), while the resurrection of the unbeliever will be delayed for 1,000 years during which he will be in chains and in torment in "hell" waiting to be cast it into "hell fire" after the White Throne Judgment.

The resurrection of the believers when Christ shall appear in the cloud is known as the First Resurrection, while the resurrection of the unbelievers 1,000 years later is called the Second Resurrection. The First Resurrection is blessed and glorious, while the Second Resurrection only leads to eternal damnation in the hell fire (Rev. Chapter 20).

The next important question to determine is who are to appear at this judgment, that is, who will be judged, what is their identity?

The Great White Throne Judgment was described by John in the Revelation as follows: "And I saw a great white throne and Him who sat on it from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away. And there was found no place for them. And I saw the dead, small and great, standing before God, and books were opened. And another book was opened, which is the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their works by the things which were written in the books. And the sea gave up the dead who were in it and death and hades delivered up the dead who were in them. And they were judged, each one according to his works. And death and hades were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And anyone not found written in the Book of Life was cast into the lake of fire". (Rev. 20:11-15).

From this passage we immediately see the identity of those judged at the Great White Throne Judgment. They are "the dead, small and great".

They are dead in sins and trespasses; but their greatest sin was unbelief and rejection of Jesus Christ as the Lord and Saviour. John 3:18 says, "He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God"

These dead in sins were resurrected to appear for this judgment.

The 'dead' include "small and great" which shows really that God is no respecter of persons (Acts 10:34).

God, the righteous judge will judge with righteousness and truth (Psalm 96:13) without looking at people's face - whether or not they were rich or poor, physically fit or handicapped, intellectual giant or dwarf, President of a Country or a farmer, a bishop or an unbeliever - "small and great" people stand before God in the final judgment!

What a moment of anxiety! The proud would be humbled; the wise would be shamed in their apparent ignorance. Everyone would stand equal before the Lord, their maker!

Our "wise" men would most probably approach the judgment throne rehearsing the logic with which they hope to confront God. But they will not know that there will be no opportunity for question and answer session.

Some think that God will just balance their good deeds with their evil works, and if the scale of the good deeds out-weighs the evil works they would be saved. There would be no such mathematical balancing and equation before God.

Other "wise" men would stand before God relying on their so-called righteous works to save them, when God has said that He regards such works as "filthy rags" (Isaiah 64:6).

Some of the people will argue in their mind: "but I was good, kind, wonderful, excellent; I treated everybody nicely and decently; I was a very active member of my church; I paid my tithe and built a church for my town; I gave regularly to the Bishop, and Pastor of my church. I was baptised when I was only three months old, and I attended church every Sunday till my death. I received holy communion, and preached many sermons in large cathedrals and crusades".

In the mind of such "wise" men it would only be the murderers, fornicators, adulterers, and other criminals that would be condemned. Little would they know that the sin of unbelief is even more deadly than the crimes enumerated.

No unconfessed sin is too small for God to send anyone to hell.

Many bishops, arch-bishops, pastors, evangelists, and others like them standing in disbelief before God at the Great White Throne judgment would then raise their voice and call, "Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in your name, cast out demons in your name, and done many wonderful works in your name?"

And the Lord would answer them saying: 'I never knew you; depart from me, you workers of iniquity'. He will then remind them saying: "Not everyone, who says to Me, Lord, Lord, will enter the Kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of My Father, who is in heaven". (Matt. 7:21-23).

These big names and titles in the christian religion would be condemned and cast into hell fire because they had not been born again. Christ told Nicodemus in John 3:3 that "Except a man be born again, he cannot see the Kingdom of God". He said further that "Except a man be born of water and of the spirit he cannot enter into the kingdom of God" (John 3:5).

"Water" here does not refer to baptism of water, but it means the word of God (Eph. 5:26) which is first preached and heard, and the Holy Spirit which acts upon it to convict the sinner who then repents, forsakes, and confesses his sins, and receives the new birth.

It is unfortunate that a preponderant number of those who attend our traditional Christian churches today are not yet born again. You ask some of them whether they are yet born again, some of them will rebuke you for asking the question, others will nicely tell you that they are not, and that they do not want to be.

Some of them do swear that they would never change anything until they die. Of course death in that condition means going to hell and we must normally have pity and compassion on such "wise" and unbelieving people knowing that their end is destruction.

There is a clear indication in Revelation 20:12 that the judgment of the unbelievers will be based on what is written in some books. It said that "the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books according to their works".

One of the books is called the Book of Life, the other is the LAMB'S BOOK OF LIFE. The Book of Life contains the names of all living people, while the LAMB'S BOOK OF LIFE in Revelation 13:8 includes only the names of those saved by the blood of Jesus, that is, those who called on the name of the Lord and were saved.

The LAMB'S BOOK OF LIFE contains names of those who received eternal life through Jesus Christ. Others who try to receive Salvation through keeping the Law will not have their names in this Book. Another Book used in the judgment contains the record of deeds done in the flesh.

The existence of this third Book of Deeds suggests that everything a person does in this life is recorded. It is said in Ecclesiastes 12:14, "For God shall bring every work into judgment with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil". Every action, behaviour, and spoken words of every person shall be recalled exposed as well as "every secret thing".

Could it be therefore that every living person has an angel of God following him and recording every thought, word, or deed of the individual every moment of his life? This must make everyone shudder at the knowledge that every word, thought, and every action of the individual is recorded by God.

This is not surprising because the Bible says, "The eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to show himself strong on behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him" (2 Chron. 16:9). Therefore no one should ever expect that he will get away with any act of wickedness he has committed in this life.

God is not only looking after the murderers, big time cheats, fornicators and adulterers to punish them, but He will also punish even such small things as backbiting, whispering, covenant-breaking, boasting, and those who invent evil things (Romans 1:30-31). No sin is too small before God.

The only person who can escape God's judgment and punishments is one who is covered in the blood of Jesus. God even said He will punish every idle word we have spoken: "But I say unto you that every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment" (Matt. 12:36). Whatever a man sows in this life he will also reap. "Be not deceived; God is not mocked; for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap" (Gal. 6:7).

The judgment at the Great White Throne will be thorough, without any mistakes because the Righteous Judge Himself will sit on the Throne and will judge in righteousness and in truth.

The three Books we have identified shall be used at the same time. Revelation 20:15 points out the importance of the Book of Life, it says: "And whosoever was not found written in the Book of life was cast in the lake of fire", and this book is for the purpose of a double-checking to ensure there is no last minute hitch or error.

The procedure at the Great White Throne Judgment may go like this: A man comes forward, he is judged by the Book of Law, as it is written in Romans 2:12 "For as many as have sinned without law will also perish without law, and as many as have sinned in the law will be judged by the law".

If the man is found guilty according to the Book of Law, he is judged by the LAMB'S BOOK OF LIFE and if his name is not there, which means he is found guilty, then he is judged by the deeds done in his flesh as contained in the Book of Deeds.

If he is equally found wanting and therefore guilty, just before he is cast into the lake of fire, he will be given the last double check. The Righteous judge shall look through the BOOK OF LIFE, "and whosoever was not found written in the Book of life was cast into the lake of fire" (Rev. 20:15).

Nobody is going to argue with anyone on that day. It will be a question of checking the Books to see if your name is there or not. If your name is in the BOOK OF LIFE you will not even appear at the Great White Throne Judgment because you would have been judged for your reward at the Judgment Seat of Christ among the saved souls.

But if your name is not in the Book of Life, it means that it was blotted out and you would therefore continue your journey into eternity in the hell fire prepared for those "workers of iniquity" and those who refused to receive the new birth.

I should add an important note here. It is not necessary that people should pray after they received Christ for God to add their names in the BOOK OF LIFE. Everybody who ever lived here on earth has his name already written in the Book of Life because God is not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance (2 Peter 3:9).

The person's name will remain in the Book of Life until at the time of his death. If at the time of his death he had received Jesus as his Lord and Saviour (if he lived in the Christian Dispensation), then his name will not be blotted out.

In Revelation 3:5 it is stated that "He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot his name out of the book of Life". However if at the time of his death he had not received Jesus (assuming he lived in the Christian Dispensation) as his Lord and Saviour, then he must have died in his sins, and his name would automatically be blotted out of the Book of Life.

In Exodus 32:33 "The Lord said unto Moses, whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book".

sections.title: Identity of the Judge
sections.html:
We have so far talked about the time of the judgment of the Great White Throne Judgment as well as the identity of those who will appear at the Judgment.

We have also seen the procedure which the Judgment may take and the nature of the BOOKS which will feature at the Judgment. We will now turn attention to even a much more important consideration, which is the JUDGE Himself.

Paul, the Apostle tells us in Acts 17:30-31 that "the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men everywhere to repent; Because he hath appointed a day in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead".

From this passage we know that God will judge the world on a day which He has already appointed. Furthermore, we are told that the judgment will be a righteous one and will be by "that man" whom God hath ordained. Not only hath God ordained "that man" but He hath also given assurance of this fact by raising Him from the dead.

Now we know that our Lord Jesus Christ is the only man in the history of this world who properly fits the description in this passage. He is "that man" who could only judge the world in righteousness because He is the only man who ever lived and committed no sin.

We are not however left in ignorance as to the proper identity of this Godly Judge. Our Lord, Himself admitted that it is in His hands that God the Father hath committed the judgment of the world: "For the Father judgeth no one, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son" (John 5:22).

The conclusion of the matter then is that the Righteous Judge (Rev. 19:11) who sits on the Great White Throne, as well as the Judge at the Judgment Seat of Christ, is one and the same person, our Lord Jesus Christ Himself. In Hebrews 4:12-13 we are told that He is a discerner of the "thoughts" and "intents" of the heart.

"Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and open unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do". Christ Himself also assured that "there is nothing covered that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known" (Matt. 10:26).

We have seen from the Bible that our Lord Jesus Christ will be the Judge both of the quick and the dead, and the Judge both of the righteous and the unrighteous. He will sit both at the Judgment Seat of Christ and at the Great White Throne when he will deal finally with all those who refused to accept Him as their Lord and personal Saviour.

There are still great many people today, even among the so-called christians who have not regarded our Lord Jesus Christ as God.

Yet when you consider the fact that it is the Lord Jesus who will judge the whole world on the Last Day, and also the fact that "all things were made by him and without him was not anything made that was made" (John 1:3) you will be left with the inescapable conclusion that the Lord Jesus Christ is God who is all in all; He liveth and reigneth together with the Father and the Holy Spirit ever one God world without end.

It is in him that "dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily" (Col. 2:9).

It is therefore the Lord Jesus Christ who created everything (John 1:3), "For by Him were all things created that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible.
