Whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things and by Him all things consist" (Col. 1:16-17). And it is He who will judge every creature (2 Cor. 5:10; Rom. 14:10 and Rev. 20:10-15, John 5:22).

What a wonderful knowledge. And what a stumbling block and bad news for them who do not believe!

sections.title: Jesus is Lord, He is God
sections.html:
There are several concrete and cogent reasons why Jesus Christ is God:

  • God is Eternal. Jesus Christ is Eternal. Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am" (John 5:58). "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, said the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty (Rev. 1:8; Also Col. 1:17).

  • God is Unchangeable. Jesus Christ is Unchangeable. "Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and today, and for ever" (Heb. 13:8).

  • God can do Everything (Omnipotent). Jesus can do Everything (Omnipotent). "And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth" (Matt. 28:18). "What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him" (Mark 4:41).

  • God is Everywhere (Omnipresent). Jesus Christ is Everywhere (Omnipresent). "And, lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world (Matt. 28:20). "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them" (Matt. 18:20).

  • God knows Everything (Omniscient). Jesus Christ knows Everything (Omniscient). "But when Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answering said unto them, What reason ye in you hearts?" (Luke 5:22). "But Jesus did not commit himself unto them, because he knew all men. And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man" (John 2:24-25).

  • God is Holy. Jesus Christ is Holy. "... I know thee who thou art, the Holy one of God" (Mark 1:24). "Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth" (1 Peter 2:22).

  • God is Just. Jesus Christ is Just. Christ in the act of cleansing the Temple (John 2:14-17), and Christ a Righteous Judge (Acts 17:31).

  • God is Loving. Jesus Christ is Loving. "Then said the Jews, Behold how he loved him!" (John 11:36). "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends" (John 15:13).

  • God is Merciful. Jesus Christ is Merciful. "Christ died for us" (Romans 5:8). "Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us" (Titus 3:5).

  • God is Faithful. Jesus Christ is Faithful. "If we deny him, he also will deny us: if we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself" (2 Tim. 2:12-13).

  • God is the Creator. Jesus is the Creator. "All things were made by Him, and without Him was not any-thing made that was made" (John 1:3; Also Heb. 1:2).

  • God is the Preserver of all things. Jesus is the Preserver of all things. "Who being the brightness of God's glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high" (Heb. 1:3).

  • God forgives sin. Jesus Christ forgives sin. "And he said unto her, Thy sins are forgiven" (Luke 7:48).

  • God raises the dead. Jesus Christ raises the dead. 'And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day" (John 6:39).

  • God is the Judge. Jesus Christ is the Judge. "For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son (John 5:22).

The Bible teaches that there is but one God and that there are three persons in one God: God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit.

Christ Himself taught this in His Great Commission to His disciples, saying, "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost" (Matt. 28:19).

Jesus Christ, the Son, claimed that He is one with the Father: "I and My Father are One" (John 10:30). He also told Philip, "He that hath seen Me hath seen the Father" (John 14:9). In John 14:1, He said, "ye believe in God, believe also in me".

Obviously the Father and the Son are one and the same, indivisible. Jesus is the image of the invisible God (Col. 1:15). Even God the Father called the Son "God" in Hebrews 1:8 "But unto the Son He (the Father) saith, Thy Throne, O God, is for ever and ever".

Note, however, that Jesus in human form took a lower position to God the Father.

He said, "My Father is greater than I" (John 14:28). But at the end of His earthly mission Christ prayed to God the Father to restore Him to His original Godly position. "And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was" (John 17:5).

Before Christ came to this world He was one with God the Father (John 10:30). And after His earthly life, glorious resurrection, and ascension, He resumed His original oneness with God the Father (Heb. 12:2).

But the divine relationship between God the Father, and the Son will not be finally resolved or manifested until we reach the point described in 1 Cor. 15:28.

The functional and positional relationship between God the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit has always engendered controversy and misunderstanding among religious groups - some denying and others professing the doctrine of one God in three persons (Trinity).

But I believe it is a sheer hypocrisy for anyone to infer that belief in Trinity means a belief in the existence of three Gods.

Trinity has always been held to mean a belief in ONE GOD who manifests Himself in three persons in His functions as God the Father (in creation); God the Son (Emmanuel); and God the Holy Ghost (the Comforter, the Spirit of Truth).

The doctrine of Trinity is biblical. Both our Lord Jesus and the early Apostolic writers including John, Peter, and Paul taught it and believed it.

So, it is not up to a christian to deny the true words, teaching, or commandments of our Lord Jesus Christ.

There are many references as to Trinity in the Bible although the word itself is not to be found in the Holy Book.

First in Matt. 28:19 Christ commanded his disciples "... baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost". ("name" as used here means "authority" i.e. in the "authority" of the Father, Son, and the Holy Ghost. See Dake's Annotated Reference Bible, p. 34).

Secondly, John 14:26 says, "But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you". And verse 28 says, "... If ye loved me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father: for my Father is greater than I".

Thirdly, John 15:26 says, "But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me".

Fourth, 2 Cor. 13:14 says, "The grace of the Lord Jesus, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all"

Fifth, 1 John 5:7 says "For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one".

Sixth, 1 Peter 1:2 says "Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ".

All these six Bible references or passages support the teaching or the doctrine of God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost (Trinity).

But there are some christians today who deny this biblical teaching on Trinity saying that anyone who believes on God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost thereby believes in the existence of three Gods.

These people say that although Jesus spoke on the Trinity (Matt. 28:19) but that Peter, speaking through the Holy Ghost later denied the doctrine in Acts 2:38.

But it is now clear that Peter did not contradict Christ. In fact he re-stated the doctrine himself in 1 Peter 1:2. All it means is that when it comes to baptism it can be done according to Matt. 28:19 as Jesus taught; or according to 1 Peter 1:2.

Both requirements are two sides of the same coin. The provision in the two passages reinforce not contradict each other. The Bible does not contain contradictions.

Then, when Mary was being briefed about the plan of God for her, and of the baby she would bear, the Angel said that He would be a "Son" and His name shall be called "JESUS": "that he shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the Throne of his father David" (Luke 1:31-32).

Another Bible passage that clearly shows Jesus as a person distinct from the Father is Philippians 2:8-9 "And (Jesus) being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also had highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name".

And 1 Cor. 15:28 says, "And when all things shall be subdued unto him (Jesus), then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him (the Father) that put all things under him, that God may be all in all"

All the above Bible references confirm that the doctrine of Trinity is biblical. But there is no doubt whatsoever that this doctrine is still shrouded in mystery (1 Tim. 3:16).

But rather than try to explain or understand a mystery of God we should instead apply the Scriptures in Deut. 29:29 that "the secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever . . ."

Any revelation that runs counter to the expressly written Word of God should not be accepted without scrutiny. The spirit of such a revelation should be subjected to the test in 1 John 4:1 because "many false prophets are gone out into the world".

Every christian should endeavour "to live by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God" (Matt. 4:4).

According to the Word of God, I believe that there is only one God and Jesus Christ is both Lord and God. Whether Jesus Christ is God the Father as well as the Son, the Bible is silent. It is a mystery. (Deut. 29:29, 1 Tim. 3:16).

But the Bible says that Jesus created everything, visible and invisible (John 1:3, 10). Jesus Christ will also judge everybody, dead or alive on the last day (John 5:22).

I also believe that Jesus manifested Himself on earth and called Himself the Son of God (Matt. 26:64, John 10:36).

Jesus Himself commanded us to "go into all nations teaching them and baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost" (Matt. 28:19). Whether God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost are three persons in One, or three functions, is a mystery of godliness (1 Tim. 3:16).

It is safer that we stand on the expressly written Word of God. We should believe Jesus in the words He spoke and which are written concerning His relationship with the Father and the Holy Spirit (Matt. 28:19, See also John 16:23 "Verily, verily, I say unto you, whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it to you".

We should also believe the written Word of God examined here and which clearly states that there is God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost, ever one God world without end.

Even on the morning of His Resurrection, our Lord sent a message to His disciples saying, "I ascend unto my Father, and your Father, and to my God, and your God" (John 20:17).

The Lord Jesus Christ said here that He has a Father and He has a God to whom He must ascend. If these things were not so He would have told us as He said in the case of the "many mansions" in His Father's house (John 14:2).

People who call themselves christians (which means "followers of Christ") must learn to believe God's Word because "He is not a man that He should lie, neither the Son of man that He should repent" (Numbers 23:19 and Heb. 6:18).

Lastly, we are warned in Rev. 22:18 not to add to or take away from the Bible. And this warning applies particularly to those who would want to take the Trinity out of the Bible.

People at different places testified as to the Lordship of Jesus Christ as well as to His deity. Thomas in John 20:28 exclaimed unto Him, "My Lord and my God".

If Christ is not God, He would have rebuked Thomas for giving Him an honour not due unto Him by calling Him God. Furthermore, at our Lord's crucifixion "when the centurion, and they that were with him, watching Jesus, saw the earthquake, and those things that were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God" (Matt. 27:54)

Also when there was dissension following Christ's teaching in the Temple, the Chief Priests and Pharisees took counsel to arrest Him and to do away with Him. They therefore sent some officers to go and arrest Jesus but when they got there they could not lay hands upon Him. Then the Chief Priests and Pharisees asked the officers, saying 'Why have ye not brought him?' They answered, "'Never man spake like this man'" (John 7: 45-46).

This is the confession of men who saw Jesus, the Lord, in action. It was true then; it is true today, and it will remain true for ever, that never has any man spoken like Jesus because no man has ever been God as Jesus was, and is, and shall be world without end.

We have seen that it is Jesus who created us and it is He who will judge us at the end. Because Christ as man "became obedient unto death", even the death of the cross, "Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father" (Phil. 2:8-11). God has therefore decided that every knee must bow to Jesus's name and every tongue must confess Him to be the Lord.

It is either you bow and confess in this life and go to heaven; or you refuse to do so now and be thrown into hell fire where you will not only be tormented day and night but must at the same time be bowing to Jesus and be confessing Him to be the Lord.

So, whether you worship, and confess, and bow to Jesus in the hell fire, or whether you do that in heaven is a decision everyone must make in this life. And that decision must be made today.

It is both risky and dangerous to delay the decision to accept the Lord Jesus because "no one knows tomorrow" as they say it.

Salvation is readily available to anyone who wants it. "Behold, now is the accepted time: behold, now is the day of salvation" (2 Cor. 6:2). Christ will surely receive anyone who comes unto Him because He has promised, saying, "... and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out" (John 6:37).

This is God's promise to mankind and when God promises anything He does it "for he is faithful that promised" (Heb. 10:23). and it is "impossible for God to lie" (Heb. 6:18).

The last evidence we shall look at which conclusively proves that Jesus Christ, the Son of Man, is also the Son of God, is the fact of His resurrection from the dead.

Paul said in Acts 17:31 that God hath "appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained: whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that HE HATH RAISED HIM FROM THE DEAD".

The evidence that Jesus is "that man" whom God hath appointed to judge the world is the fact that God raised Him from the dead.

Furthermore, in a most powerful air of assurance and confidence, our Lord Jesus referred to His life, death, and resurrection saying; "As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep. . . Therefore doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again. . . No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I HAVE POWER TO LAY IT DOWN, AND I HAVE POWER TO TAKE IT AGAIN. This commandment have I received of my Father" (John 10:15, 17-18).

Thus we know that Christ is all powerful, omnipotent. Any person who could heal all manner of diseases, made the blind to see, the lame to walk, healed the leper, cast out evil spirits, raised the dead, that person is God, and Christ who did all that and more, He is surely God!

But He did not just raise others who died, rather He said, "I have power to lay down my life and I have power to take it again". He did not just say it in words, He demonstrated His Word in Great Power and Might.

Praise the Lord! There is something else Christ said, He said that His Resurrection from the dead was a "Commandment" which He received from the Father. When God has commanded, who is there to argue?

Christ, my all in all, to Him be all glory and honour, praise and thanksgiving, worship, power and majesty, dominion, blessings and excellence, both now and for ever more!

The issue of resurrection has been the most controversial and yet it is on it that the Christian faith and hope for eternal life in heaven hinge.

Throughout ages some people particularly the worldly "wise" have argued that death would end the existence of man on earth and that there is nothing like life after death, or resurrection from the dead.

The Sadducees who lived in the time of our Lord Jesus denied there is any resurrection (Luke 20:27); Also the "wise" people from among the philosophers of the Epicureans and the Stoics when they heard Paul preach at Athens about Jesus and resurrection of the dead, "some mocked" (Acts 17:18, 32).

There are also some that Paul complained of in 1 Cor. 15:12 who said that "there is no resurrection of the dead".

And in 2 Timothy 2:18 Paul specifically mentioned two men: Hymenaeus and Philetus who went about teaching that resurrection is a past thing already; that if resurrection is possible it was possible in the days past not now and not in future.

Paul said that because of this teaching they "overthrow the faith of some".

But the truth of the matter is that God has always manifested His power through resurrection of the dead. There are several examples:

  • Son of the widow of Zarephat (1 Kings 17:22).

  • The Son of the Shunamite woman (2 Kings 4:35).

  • Dead man restored to life at the touch of Elijah's bones (2 Kings 13:21).

  • Jairus daughter (Matt. 9:25, Mark 5:42).

  • The Saints at the time of crucifixion (Matt. 27:52).

  • The Son of the widow of Nain (Luke 7:15).

  • Lazarus of Bethany (John 11:44).

  • Dorcas (Acts 9:40).

If God raised all these from the dead, why should there be doubt that the same God raised His only begotten Son, Jesus Christ from the dead.

The Resurrection of Christ was foretold: it did not come by any surprise.

  • In Psalm 49:15 "But God will redeem my soul from the power of the grave: for he shall receive me" (Also Psalm 16:10, 71:20, Hosea 13:14).

  • In Matt. 16:21 "From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day".

  • Matt. 26:32 "But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee".

  • Mark 9:9 "And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen till the son of man were risen from the dead" (see also John 2:19; Acts 26:22-23).

Evidence that Christ rose from the dead abound. There is the evidence of the empty tomb, although some detractors say that our Lord's body was removed either by friends or enemies. But that cannot be because if enemies took the body they would have produced it when Peter preached his first sermon in Acts 2:14-47.

When Peter told them in verse 32, that, "this Jesus hath God raised up", the supposed enemies who took the body would have tried to disprove the message of the Apostle by producing the body. Or if "friends" of Jesus had stolen the body as some argue, then the disciples (the "friends" of Jesus) could not have been surprised or even doubted the message of Mary that Christ had risen.

When the women who went to the grave saw the empty tomb, they came back and narrated the story to the eleven disciples, the Bible says: "And their words seemed to them (the eleven disciples) as idle tales, and they believed them not" (Luke 24:10-11).

Apart from the evidence of the empty tomb there is also the fact of the appearances of our Lord after His resurrection. There is a record of eleven appearances and most of the people were alive when some of the gospel accounts were written.

If the story of the appearances were false some of these people who were not even disciples would have refuted the story.

They would have been happy to say that their names were being misused in blaspheming God, and in saying that God raised up somebody whom He did not raise up.

But there was no such counter testimony which shows that the Bible account is correct, and genuine. The story of the resurrection appearances of our Lord will be found in the following passages: (Matt. 27:57-28:20); (Mark 15:42-16:20); (Luke 23:50-24:53); (John 19:38-21:25); and (1 Cor. 15).

But we thank God that Paul gave a definite answer in 1 Cor. 15:20, "But now is Christ risen from the dead". If Christ did not rise from the dead it would be a calamity for Christians in so many ways (1 Cor. 15):

  • We will have no guarantee of our own resurrection (verses 12-13; 20-23);

  • Our preaching would be in vain (verse 14);

  • Our faith would be in vain (verse 14, 17);

  • We are liars; because we have preached that Jesus rose (verse 15);

  • We are yet in our sins (verse 17);

  • All the dead are perished (verse 18);

  • We have no hope (verse 19);

  • We are miserable (verse 19);

  • We are plain fools (verses 30-32);

  • Nature is a farce (verses 35-49);

  • Promises are lies (verses 50-54);

  • Prophecies are false (verses 55-56);

But now we know that the resurrection of Christ is a fact and it is that fact which guarantees the resurrection of all other men who die in the Lord (verses 20-22).

If Christ were a fake, or a liar, an impostor, or merely a superman, God would have left Him to decay in the grave and would resurrect Him on the Day of Judgment and then condemn Him to hell fire.

But God did not do that. Instead, according to Paul in Romans 6:4, it was God the Father Himself, who raised Christ, His only begotten Son, from the dead and thus Christ "became the first fruits of them that slept" (verse 20).

And because Christ arose so we must arise because it is Christ in us the hope of glory (Col. 1:27).

sections.title: My Life and My Salvation
sections.html:
In concluding this work, I will delve into some more personal salvation experiences in the hope that one can learn the lesson that what God has done in one person He can also do in others because from everlasting to everlasting He is God (Psalm 90:2); and Jesus Christ, the same yesterday, and today, and for ever (Heb. 13:8).

I was born into a traditional christian family at Uli in Anambra State. My father (Benjamin) was one of the first Lay-Readers of the church and in that capacity he took active and leadership role in the church both at the town and at the District or Parish levels.

The Church building in which we worshipped stood and still stands about twenty yards away from my compound that some people have often mistaken the compound to be part of the church parsonage. I must say that the devil used the nearness of my house to the church to try to work against my conversion as will be seen later.

In any case, I grew up in the best christian tradition and training. I was baptised about three months after birth when as yet I knew not God nor what the Word of God says about salvation and baptism. But because infant baptism was part of the doctrine and tradition of the church I was duly initiated.

Then a few years later, I think while I was in primary six or so, I was confirmed. The Bishop laid hands on me and I started receiving the Holy Communion as a full communicant and having all the privileges, and of course responsibilities of full membership of the Church.

My father (Benjamin) and mother (Agnes) gave us (I mean myself and the other six children in the family) very good christian training. They taught us to pray every morning and every night. My father introduced competition.

After reading the Bible portion each time he would give the memory verse from the Scripture Union pamphlet which we used as a guide, and whoever found the verse first would win a prize.

The competition heightened my interest in the Bible with the result that Religious Studies became one of my best subjects in School and later in the College.

So, right from childhood, till I went into Teachers' College, graduated, became a teacher, and took the General Certificate of Education (GCE) Examination.

I had all along read the Bible, prayed with it, studied it, passed higher examinations in it, and even lectured on it. But all these were only head knowledge.

The Bible hadn't really entered my heart. I read portions of the "Holy Book" off-head, having memorized them in order to pass my examinations. I even preached in local churches as well as in the Christian College where I lectured as a tutor.

In September 1966, I left Bishop Lasbrey College where I had been teaching, and travelled to the United States having received admission from the State University of New York (New Paltz) with full scholarship of room board, tuition and fees.

I knew that this admission was God's work but I was not sure whether I received it through prayers to God, or whether I got it by applying the Rosicrucian Order (AMORC) Principles. I might mention that although I regarded myself as a very good christian, and my friends and relatives saw me too as a good christian, quiet, peaceful, with regular attendance to church, yet I was a member of the Rosicrucian Order (AMORC).

In the United States as a student, I affiliated myself with the local Episcopal Church which is like the Anglican Church in Nigeria. I prayed, and read the Bible, and there was much preaching too.

Most of the preachers in these churches dwelt more on theology, sociology and psychology. Little effort was usually made to really talk about salvation and God's provisions for it.

My studies in the United States went smoothly. In 1969 I got my B.A. (Hons) in Politics from New York; in 1970 I got the M.A. degree from Ohio University; and in 1972 I got the Ph.D. from Cornell University. Then from 1972 to 1975, I lectured as an Associate Professor of African Studies and Politics at the State University of New York (Cortland) and also became Chairman of the Academic Department.

However, in September 1975 my wife (who had just got her B.A. (Hons) in Sociology, and along with our daughter who was only five weeks old), and I, left New York for England where I took a law degree at the University of Southampton.

It was at Southampton that I was first exposed to an evangelical church, the above Bar Church, whose Rev. Minister Leith Samuel and his wife, and later Rev. David Jackman who took over from them, opened my eyes and that of my wife, to what God can do in the life of those who believe in the finished work of Jesus on the Cross of Calvary.

The members of the church were selfless and committed. The Word of God was preached in power and conviction, and christian faith was shown by its works (James 2:20).

It was during my active involvement there in Christian evangelism, prayer, and Bible teaching that I knew for the first time that it was a sin for me to be a christian and at the same time belong to the Rosicrucian Order (AMORC).

Given their practice of praying and meditating by the use of candles, mirror or glass, and crystal ball for gazing, it is clear that one cannot be a good christian and still belong to the Order.

The Bible says, "there shall not be found among you any one... to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a charmer or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. For all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord..." (Deut. 18:10-12).

As I read one of the prepared degree manuscripts of the Order one day, I came across where they wrote that Jesus Christ is one of the greatest teachers and prophets that ever lived; that He is an avater.

As regards being the "the" Son of God; that everyone can develop his faculties and brain to be "a" Son of God. So the Order did not then believe (I do not know whether they now believe) that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and that He is even God Himself.

I immediately wrote the Grand Secretary of the Order in California and asked him to explain the basis of their teaching on our Lord Jesus Christ and to show me why the Bible teaching about His deity should not supersede the AMORC teaching on the subject.

I did not hear again from the Order and immediately thereafter I wrote them to discontinue my membership. I had nothing against the Order except for their teaching on the Lord Jesus Christ which denies His deity.

By the time I left the Order I had got to the highest point of membership having been awarded the degree and status of FELLOW OF THE ROSE CROSS (FRC). But I thank God for delivering me from their hands and I have now done with their books, candles and incense, and other materials what the Bible says in Acts 19:18-20.

In September 1977 my family left England and returned to Nigeria. I had become a "reformed" christian. At that stage in 1977 I was not yet a born again christian. I was still a church goer.

But as a result of my exposure at the Above Bar Church in Southampton, I became a 'renovated' christian but there was yet no 'revolution' which is the new birth.

At that stage I knew a lot about Jesus Christ. I knew all about His birth, miracles, teachings, death, resurrection and ascension and His promise of second coming. I was quite satisfied at my level of involvement in matters of christianity and I never wanted to be more or less active.

Back home in Nigeria, I first took up a job with the Daily Times as Foreign Affairs Correspondent and later became editor of "Times International".

After my training in the Nigerian Law School in June 1979, I was called to the Nigerian Bar as Solicitor and Advocate. In September of that year I was given appointment by the Anambra State Governor as the General Manager of Daily Star Printing and Publishing Company, Enugu, which is a State Government Company.

Later I was given a new post as Director of Planning and Research in the Governor's Office. From there I resigned in June 1980. In September of the same year I was appointed the Special Assistant to the Country's Vice President, in charge of Political and Administrative Matters at the State House, Ribadu Road, Lagos.

While I served in all these successive political posts, I was still attending churches every Sunday, but it was more as a social than christian obligation. I was not quite alive to the things of the spirit.

God took secondary position. Politics being the art of the possible meant that the end will always justify the means. I never regarded things like cheating and lying as sin. Or in any case I was sure God will not be concerned with "small" sins like lying when there are armed robbers and people like that. I

n any case, sin was not in my dictionary at that time.

I regarded actions like cheating and lying as being smart and being wise. I thought that it was only people with the fastest brain who could successfully cheat and manipulate to get their way through.

I felt that the brain God gave us should be used to get whatever we wanted by any means necessary. I was in fact walking on the broad way that leads to destruction, but my eyes were closed to this fact.

But despite all these shortcomings and unrighteousness I still felt I was better than many, and that I still had a chance for heaven because I was already baptised and I did receive the holy communion.

And then I started to reason that if God did not love me how would I get these high political positions? If I were a sinner, why would God help me to get all the degrees, and be placed on these top posts, one after the other? Why would God prosper me if I did not do the will of God?

These were questions passing through my mind.

I saw no reason for repentance and it baffled me when the Pentecostal or evangelical christians urged me to repent and receive Christ.

I used to ask them, "Does it mean that since my childhood I hadn't received Christ, when I had always been a christian and attended church regularly? I gave alms to the poor, contributed to church buildings, became chairman of harvest committee, sang in the choir, played on the organ? Why should any one ask me to repent? What is there for me to repent of?"

Furthermore, the implication of saying that I have repented only now is that I would be admitting that all these years I had been a "christian" were wasted years; and it was a most difficult admission to make. I thought people would just think that I was foolish and unreasonable.

I used to tell those who preached to me that I was doing my best trying to keep the laws and commandments and that I loved God, and loved my neighbours as myself, which Christ said is the summary of all the laws and the prophets (Matt. 22:37-40). I felt that since God knows the heart He will know those who are trying.

I thought that as long as I was making effort to live well and to keep the ten commandments that I would make it to heaven: after all, if I could keep six out of the ten commandments that would make a pass mark. And in any case, I felt it was safer for me to remain with the majority always. There was no need to go to the extreme in anything.

I asked myself why I should be that kind of a christian who goes to people to worry them about repentance. Why should I see somebody, who says he is already a christian and I begin to ask him to repent, and to receive Christ? How many times shall a christian receive Christ in his life?

I just felt that everything about church and christianity should be kept in the heart and be made a personal matter. Nobody should preach to another except you are a pastor, and even if you are a pastor, you should find a church and not preach anywhere on the street or disturb people in their homes.

This was the way I thought about the whole issue of christianity until one day.

So there was this particular day in November, 1983, the news reached me that my younger brother, Kenneth, who along with my mother, had been preaching to me to repent, was reported to have gone to be with the Lord

He was the person more than others, who really "bothered" and "worried" me with this matter of repentance. Anywhere he saw me he must open up the question of salvation and the new birth.

At times I would argue with him, but at times when I didn't have time for argument I would just agree with him that the penticostals are all holy people and that I was convinced they are all going to heaven!

Each time I came home from Lagos on a weekend he timed me so well that he had always come home too. Then 5.00 am. every morning he would knock at my door for family morning prayers and I would scream and complain, and ask them to go ahead that I would pray when I get up.

My mother would also come to my bedside to preach and pray, and I would promise her that I had repented but that she should just allow me to sleep first. The next morning I would assure her that I had repented but that I would like to remain in my old Church. She wouldn't give up.

But on this November day on which Kenneth had gone to be with the Lord, the whole of the Church in which he had been an Elder, assembled on my compound. The praises they sang were very inspirational.

Music has a way of bringing the best out of me and the Church chorale, accompanied with assorted musical instruments, and rendered by the Church band, called the Grace Band, brought a lot of grace to me, and peace to my mind.

Then also was the preaching. God knew what He wanted to use that occasion to accomplish in my life. Simply stated, I had heard few preachings made in such a tremendous power, authority and conviction before.

The young men God used at the occasion were Rev. Paul C. Nweke (Nwachukwu), Rev. Augustine A. Nwodika and Rev. Benjamin Ikedinobi all of the Grace of God Mission in Nigeria, a penticostal, evangelical church.

Before these preachers finished their messages that day, I was completely broken down. Soaked in tears, I have never been the same again.

The tears were not just for my brother whom I knew already had gone to be with the Lord, but I cried for all the years I lived in utter disobedience to the Word of God.

That day I got an immediate revelation that the Bible is the Word of God and that what God says He will do He will surely do it. My tears were tears of joy because if I myself had died a day before, I would have died in my sins.

But for me, the day of burying my brother was the "accepted time", behold, it was the "day of salvation" (2 Cor. 6:2). It was the day God chose to bring salvation to my door steps. Thus since the proverbial Mountain couldn't go to Mohammed, Mohammed had to go the Mountain.

The Gospel "Mountain" to which I couldn't go rather came to me that day because if my brother had not left, the Church would not have gathered in my house, and I would not have had the opportunity to hear the gospel, and without hearing there would be no faith, and without faith there could be no salvation.

But I thank God that it pleased Him that I should receive the new birth that day. I was surely born again with water and the spirit (John 3:5) and the joy of salvation filled my heart because "old things are passed away and behold all things are become new" (2 Cor. 5:17).

Suddenly, the sorrows and the burden of my brother's death changed into a life of testimony of what the Lord has done for me in giving me a new life. God in His infinite wisdom and mercy withdrew one life and gave back another one.

May His Holy Name be Praised! And as for my brother, Kenneth, Christ was magnified in his body both by his life and by his death (Phil. 1:20).

The Bible tells me that there is hell, and there is heaven as we have examined in this study and I believe it. The Bible also tells me that except I am born again that I shall not see the kingdom of God (John 3:3), and it also says that unless I am born again with water and the spirit I will go to hell. I also believe the Bible.

The Bible is the Word of God and when once God has spoken it is final because "God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it; or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?" (Numbers 23:19).

There is no doubt that although I have read the Bible all the years past and have heard the word of God, but at the "due time", (Titus 1:3), at the "fulness of time" and at "the time appointed of the Father" (Galatians 4:2, 4).

God manifested His love towards me and fulfilled His plan of my salvation which He made before the foundation of the earth. It was not everyone who heard the gospel message that day repented.

Many who were there that day probably only took notice of the fine acrobatic movements and gestures of the preachers as they demonstrated the points of their messages. To such people the whole thing would just have been another aspect of a funeral entertainment taking the place of masquerade displays.

Such people were not saved, just as those who went with Saul of Tarsus did not themselves receive the heavenly vision given to Saul on the road to Damascus. But I heard the message, faith came, and I was saved! The Bible says that "faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the Word of God" (Rom. 10:17).

With my salvation now fully secured by grace through faith, not of myself, but the gift of God, not of works, I can look back and see the chequered way through which I passed to get where I am now.

The first weapon the devil used to fight against my conversion was the fact of geographical proximity of my house to the old Church where I worshipped in my home. The devil asked why repentance should mean leaving my "father's church" built inside the premises of my compound.

But I reminded the opponents that there is nothing like one "inheriting" ones father's church or religion. The freedom of choice is always available and one should choose a church according to which church can satisfy one's spiritual longings.

The churches where sermons deal with mainly social and political problems and where denominational doctrines and traditions weigh more than the Word of God (the Bible), must be rejected.

The Church that is recommended is one where the Word of God comes first in every consideration; where the new birth and salvation are preached, and where holiness is a way of life. God commanded us saying "Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord" (Heb. 12:14).

Those who say that it is humanly impossible to be holy in this life must therefore die in their sins and must go to hell. But they still can repent today and believe the Word of God and be saved, because it is not the will of God that any should perish but that all should come to repentance (2 Peter 3:9).

Another aspect of my life through which the devil sought to steal away my salvation was my education and the high political posts I held.

The pressure on me then was that I needed no repentance because God had already confirmed that I was His son by giving me an open door in the number of degrees I earned and the big posts I occupied.

The devil always asks people, "If you are not already going to heaven why has God given you good education, good jobs, wealth, cars, houses and things like that?" In this way the devil will deceive you and make you to remain long in your sins because he tells you that worldly prosperity is an indication that you are either in heaven already, or you will definitely get there because God loves you.

Satan would ask you saying "If God could give you all you need here in this life how can He deny you eternal life in heaven?" This is devil's lies and no one should be deceived. "For we are not ignorant of Satan's devices" (2 Cor. 2:11).

Our prosperity here in this life has nothing to do with our salvation. Christ calls us and He wants us to come to Him just as we are, whether rich or poor, short or tall, ugly or beautiful, ignorant or educated.

What God wants is our heart. Rich, educated men will go to heaven; and poor, illiterate ones will also go there, depending on those whose hearts are pure towards God. Similarly, rich and educated men as well as poor illiterates will go to hell because they rejected Jesus, not because of their status here on earth.

John in his revelation saw dead men: "small and great" standing before God at the Great White Throne waiting to be judged and to be cast into the hell fire (Rev. 20:12).

It should be noted that any person who appears at the Great White Throne is destined for eternal damnation in the hell fire; and whoever appears at the Judgment Seat of Christ is already saved. Where will you appear if you die today?

The only thing that entitles you to appear at the Judgment Seat of Christ is the new birth. If not, you must appear at the Great White Throne Judgment and on that day your education, high political or social position, wealth, and everything upon which you had cast all your hopes in this world, will not help you.

All who had deceived you in this life will desert you, and you alone will face your God for worse, not for better. But this does not have to happen to you because today is the accepted time, today is the day of salvation if you should just believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and be saved (Acts 16:31).

Another point of attack by the enemy was my previous christian background and up-bringing. The enemy kept reminding me that I was already baptised and confirmed, and that there was nothing left for me to do in order to enter the Kingdom of heaven.

What the devil is interested in are the formalities, the shadow, not the substance. God commands us to "repent and be baptised" (Acts 2:38); but the devil says no; the proper order is for you to be baptized first, and then you don't even need any repentance because the "infant" baptism is just enough to wipe away all your sins.

Many people choose to believe the lies of the devil than the true Word of God.

Some church-goers would tell you that the evidence they are saved is that God answers their prayers. They are very much deceived. God said that He watches after His Word to perform it, (Jer. 1:12) so that if someone prays according to God's will He will honour His word and will answer the prayer.

But God's answer to our prayers does not mean we are saved; it does not even mean that we live right with God. People who rely on their prayers, their good works, and works of their own hands for salvation should remember the case of Cornelius.

The Bible says that "Cornelius, the Centurion, was a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews". He was "a devout man and feared God with all his house; he gave much alms to the people and prayed to God always" (Acts 10:1, 22).

What should be noted here is that the "prayers" and the "much alms" of Cornelius were not enough to save Him. Rather salvation came to him and his house-hold when Peter gave them the gospel message. It was the truth of the gospel which they received and which saved them, because "faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the Word of God" (Romans 10:17).

The mercy which God had for Cornelius was in sending Peter to him to give him the gospel message. Then Cornelius had a choice either to accept or reject the message. He accepted it and was saved.

Today God hears many prayers of some unbelievers and the church-goers, and He shows them mercy by sending to them the born again christians to preach to them the gospel message.

There are some who reject the gospel message but add that if God needs them as He needed Saul of Tarsus, He then could make their conversion as miraculous as that of St. Paul. It is clear that people like this are among those who are ashamed to confess Christ before men (Mark 8:38 also Matt. 10:32-33). Such people are also afraid of what people around them would say, people like father, mother, wife, husband, friends and so on (Math. 10:37).

But the "wisdom" of these people is like foolishness to God. God knows that the heart of man is "deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it", except the Lord Himself who alone can "search the heart" and "try the reins" (Jeremiah 17:9-10 and Psalm 139:23-24).

Since God knows the heart and all its imaginations no man can ever deceive Him.

People who wait for miraculous or forced conversion are not serious. They are people tightly roped into some sins and who enjoy such sins that to them it requires God to come down from heaven to "force" them to give up the sinful habits.

But God told us to repent of our sins by our own free-will. We must repent and forsake our sins. We must do this by ourselves. God will not do it for us.

We are told in Romans 6:13 to "yield ourselves unto God" and "yield your members as instruments of righteousness unto God".

This calls for a definite act of self-will on our part. We must "yield ourselves". No other person, even God, will do it for us. Christ has defeated Satan once and for all and whatever battle that remains against the devil must be fought and won by us.

He has also equipped us to fight and to win this battle against sin, and against the powers and principalities in this world.

Therefore God wants us to "be strong in the Lord, and in the power of His might", and to "put on the whole armour of God... to be able to stand against the wiles of the devil" (Ephesians 6:10-17).

For such people who are not willing to repent of their own free-will, even if God should force them into repentance, they cannot be true disciples afterwards.

After conversion they will also expect God to force them to witness for Christ. When trials and tribulations come to them as christians they cannot bear them; you will hear them blame God for ever forcing them into conversion. They would murmur and complain all the days of their lives. They would never be willing instruments in God's hands to do His will.

People who look for forced or miraculous conversion do not seek God with pure heart fervently; they only seek to deal deceitfully with God. They do not believe the Word of God, they rather seek to tempt the Lord their God and God Himself commanded us saying, "Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God" (Matt. 4:7).

However, because "with God nothing shall be impossible" (Luke 1:37), God is able to convert anyone anyhow He chooses. He at times uses His Word in the Bible; He also gives special revelation, and at other times He uses shocking events like death of loved ones, or near fatal accidents to open the gate of salvation to some people.

But it is important to note that the people God deals with in these special ways are special people who sincerely seek God, and who want to know Him and are committed to doing His will.

We can take the case of the Ethiopian Eunuch. The Bible tells us how he sat in his chariot and read a portion in Isaiah the Prophet. Although he did not understand what he read but he had a sincere heart to know the Lord.

Then Philip was sent to go and guide him and thereafter the Ethiopian believed the gospel as preached by Philip; he was born again by water and the spirit; and he was saved (Acts 8:26-39).

And even in the case of Paul, his conversion confirms the case that God does not seek, nor does He use unwilling instruments.

Paul, as Saul of Tarsus, was completely yielded to God. He had a burning zeal to do the work of God. He loved God with all his heart, with all his mind, and with all his strength. His persecution of Christians was to protect the religion of his time.

He saw christianity as a threat to the established religion-the religion of Moses, Elijah, Elisha, the great Prophets, the great Kings and the nation of Israel.

Saul of Tarsus had the zeal but he hadn't the knowledge that salvation was no longer based on law and works, but on the Saviour, Jesus Christ.

However, we noticed that Paul used all his strength, conviction, zeal, knowledge and training; he committed his life to work to preserve the Jewish religion believing he was working according to the will of God.

But because he had a sincere heart towards God, the Lord "arrested" him, miraculously converted him, and made him an instrument of honour in His hand for the preservation and propagation of the gospel throughout the whole world.

This is also the way our Lord converted and used His early disciples who were fishermen. He called them and used them as fishers of men because the zeal, perseverance, endurance and painstaking effort with which they fished (sometimes all night and got no fish) were qualities and characteristics that are necessary to "go and teach all nations" and to win souls for Christ (Math. 28:19).

People who merely sit in their palours, and drink, smoke, and engage in idle talks all the day are not the stuff God would waste His time and resources trying to give a miraculous conversion because they would never be obedient to any heavenly vision.

So my dear reader, God will not force you to be saved. The Bible already contains the steps which anyone can take to receive salvation. And if you wish, you can receive Christ today and be saved.

Like Cornelius, and like me too, some do believe the gospel message and are saved, others reject it to their peril. But again no one needs be lost. As long as we are alive there is still chance we can come to repentance and receive the free salvation which God has offered to mankind (Eph. 2:8).

But if through hesitation, doubt, and unbelief one dies without receiving Christ and without the new birth then the person should note that "it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment" (Heb. 9:27).

Another point through which the devil attacks the children of God is in witnessing. A christian is called to be a witness and to preach the Word of God everywhere and every time.

But the devil would discourage us from doing this because he knows that his Kingdom would collapse the moment more and more people receive and believe the Word.

But God said, "Ye shall teach them (the Word) to your children, speaking of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, when thou liest down, and when thou risest up. And thou shalt write them upon the door posts of thine house, and upon thine gates" (Deut. 11:19-20).

This is why christians carry gospel messages on their cars and vehicles, and write signs on their doors at home and in offices in obedience to the word of God.

The devil may tell us that we are trying too hard in the christian work. He will tell us to relax, rest a little, don't over-do it, don't be an extremist. He will tell us to follow the majority, knowing that such majority are unbelievers. But as christians who live in the spirit and walk in the spirit (Gal. 5:25), we must not accept the deceit and discouragements of the devil.

We must continue to be very active and 'hot' in the work of God, remembering the warning our Lord gave against those who are lukewarm. He said, "I know thy works, thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth" (Rev. 3:15-16).

If any christian is not active, if he is lukewarm, not hot, God will vomit him out of His mouth. This is the Word of God and it "endureth for ever" (1 Peter 1:23, 25).

It is quite clear that everyone will not be saved at last. But God will keep drawing to Himself and adding to His church daily "such as should be saved" (Acts 2:47)

Our Lord Jesus Christ also said "I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me" (John 12:32), and Peter has written too, that "God is long-suffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance" (2 Peter 3:9).

These are wonderful promises of God which men should quickly appropriate in their lives because God who promised He is able and faithful to fulfil.

The Bible has made it clear that there is no salvation in any other name "for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved" (Acts 4:12).

Christ Himself declared "I am the way, the truth, and the life no man cometh unto the Father, but by me" (John 14:6). He also commanded us, "ye believe in God, believe also in me" (John 14:1), and after we have done all these things He entreated us saying, "If ye love me, keep my commandments" (John 14:15).

The commandments the Lord wants us to keep is not the ten commandments of Moses. They include the ten but they are more than that. We are commanded to live by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God (Matt. 4:4).

Some checked and say that there are 1,050 commandments which our Lord commanded us to keep (See Dake's Annotated Reference Bible, p. 4). and He said in Matt 5:19 that, "Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the Kingdom of heaven"

May I warn finally against the greatest hinderance which people have in receiving salvation from God; this is doubt and unbelief.

Some find it very difficult to believe that the Bible is the Word of God. They say, "Suppose I believe and at last it turns out not to be? Suppose the whole gospel message turns out to be false, a fraud, or a pure human contrivance? Suppose Jesus Christ turns out not be God or even the Son of God? Suppose I take Him to be my Lord and Saviour and it turns out that salvation is not really in His name?"

They "suppose" and "suppose" and "suppose" and in that doubt, many of them die and meanwhile go to hell, and miss the whole wonderful plan of God for their salvation.

The devil uses issues and questions like these ones to becloud the minds and hearts of people, searing their conscience with hot iron as Paul rightly said, "that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of devil. Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron" (1 Tim. 4:1-2).

Some people do not believe the gospel for fear of criticism from people. They fear the reactions of wife, husband, friends, father, mother and so on. Some do not believe because repentance may mean giving up sinful habits which they are already used to in their life pattern.

Some do not believe because they fear it might lead to their changing church. They are used to attending the old church and living in sin because no one criticizes them. They are already friendly with the pastor of the church and he cannot criticize their sinful habits. They are elected chairmen of building committees, harvest committees, and so on.

They would say that the devil they know is better than the one they don't know. They therefore come to the conclusion that it is in the old church they must die and be buried. Surely they will die, but that church cannot save them. They must have died for nothing because Christ made it clear that "except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God" (John 3:3).

So my dear brothers or sisters, before you die in that your "father's church", I want you to ask yourself sincerely whether you have been born again.

Can you truly tell your friends and relatives that you are a born again christian? If you know you are not yet born again then "now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation" (2 Cor. 6:2).

Don't go to hell because of the unbelief of your wife, husband, father, mother and friend. Read Matt. 10:37-38 and note that we ought to obey God rather than men (Acts 5:29).

The Bible has continued to warn us against doubt and unbelief:

  • John 3:18 says, "He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned

  • already because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God."

  • Romans 3:4 says, "For what if some did not believe Shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar..."

  • 1 Cor. 1:18 says, "For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God."

  • 2 Tim. 2:12-13 says, "If we deny him, he also will deny us. If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself".

  • - Titus 1:15 says, "Unto the pure all things are pure but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled".

  • Hebrews 3:12 says, "Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God".

  • Hebrews 3:19 says, "So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief".

  • - Revelation 21:8 says, "But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers and idolaters, and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone".

Does this list not make you tremble? God regards unbelief or unbelievers the same way He regards a liar, a murderer, a fornicator, the adulterous, and idolaters.

As I end now I want to talk to every one of my readers the same way Christ warned His hearers in John 15:22. He told them that the gospel He had preached to them would stand as a testimony against them because, "If I had not come and spoken unto you, you had not had sin: but now you have no cloke for your sin".

God warned in Psalm 50:22 saying, "Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver".

Lastly, the Lord has also warned the born again christian, saying, "When I say unto the wicked, O wicked man, thou shalt surely die: if thou dost not speak to warn the wicked from his way; that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but his blood will I require at thine hand.

Nevertheless, if thou warn the wicked of his way, he shall die in his iniquity; but thou hast delivered thy soul" (Ezekiel 33:8-9).

So, to as many as are unbelievers and the so-called Christians who are not yet born again, I have in this book discharged the obligation my salvation placed on me to warn you about the impending doom if you should remain in your sins without repenting of them, and forsaking them, and then enter into the new birth by receiving Christ Jesus as your Lord and personal Saviour TODAY.

Now, I thank God for my salvation and that of my wife and family. I quite remember all my worldly accomplishments, my academic qualifications and achievements, my social status and the high positions I had attained in life.

But like Paul, I now "do count them but dung, that I may win Christ" (Phil. 3:8). But "not as though I had already attained, either were already perfect: but I follow after, if that I may apprehend that for which also I am apprehended of Christ Jesus.

Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I PRESS TOWARD THE MARK FOR THE PRIZE OF THE HIGH CALLING OF GOD IN CHRIST JESUS" (Phil. 3:12-14).

I believe that what God has done for me, He will do for anyone who comes to Him in sincerity and in truth for "How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation" (Heb. 2:3). YOU TOO CAN BE SAVED TODAY!
